Qatar GP: Explaining 2026 tyre-limit rule and what impact it will have on F1 race weekend at Lusail International Circuit
Why a lap limit on tyre usage is again in place at Lusail as we explain, with the help of Bernie Collins, what impact it might have on the weekend;watch every session from the Qatar GP live Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
Wednesday 25 November 2026 18:31, UK
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Look back at some of the most dramatic moments to have taken place at the Qatar Grand Prix.
Formula 1 returns to the Middle East this weekend for the first time since pre-season testing in February for back-to-back races to finish the 2026 campaign.
Qatar stages the first of those, with the fast, flowing Lusail International Circuit hosting a Grand Prix for the fifth occasion since its debut in 2021.
As was the case last year, a tyre limit regulation is in place for the race, so what is it and what impact might it have on the weekend?
Qatar GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
F1 2026 Calendar|F1 2026 Standings|F1 Gossip Column

Not got Sky?Latest Sky Sports dealsorstream F1 with no contract📺
What's the Qatar Grand Prix tyre rule for 2026?
Pirelli, Formula 1's tyre supplier, last week announced there will be a limit of 27 laps on a set of tyres for this weekend in Qatar.
It is the third time a tyre limit has been implemented for the race at the Lusail International Circuit after punctures at the inaugural 2021 event, and safety concerns being raised during the 2023 weekend.
In 2023, Pirelli mandated a three-stop race and last year they implemented a 25-lap limit which effectively created a two-stop race.
Image:Race winner Max Verstappen makes one of his two pit stops in last year's Qatar GP
The Qatar Grand Prix is 57 laps so the 27-lap limit for this weekend means, like last year, each driver will need to pit at least twice.
Pirelli explained "the increase [in the limit] has been made possible by the lower load levels recorded so far on the current generation of cars and by a further reinforcement of the tyre construction".
Laps to the grid, formation laps and laps after the chequered flag do not count towards the lap total but laps will be counted cumulatively across all track sessions.
In effect, that means if a driver does three laps on a set of tyres in qualifying, and uses those tyres in the race, they can only do another 24 laps on them before changing in the Grand Prix.
"This precautionary measure is linked to the unique characteristics of the Lusail circuit, which is particularly demanding in terms of energy loads, thermal stress and tread wear," added Pirelli.
Craig Slater gives his verdict on the Las Vegas GP where Max Verstappen claimed victory after multiple lead changes and Ferrari come together raising more dilemmas for Fred Vasseur
What will the impact of the rule be on the Qatar race weekend?
Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins, a former head of race strategy at Aston Martin, answers several of the key questions around the rule…
Bernie:"Qatar is a very high-speed track and there used to be some very aggressive, sharp-edged kerbs that led to some cuts in the sidewalls of tyres.
"That resulted in quite strong limits on the number of laps in 2023 when an 18-lap tyre limit was imposed.
"That very short limit combined with very hot conditions that year, when the race was held in October, made it very difficult for drivers. They were pushing very hard every lap in very high temperatures, which is one of the reasons why we now declare a heat hazard if it's over 31 degrees and drivers can wear a cooling vest.
Lance Stroll and Alex Albon were both seen struggling to get out of their cars from the onboard cameras at the end of a gruelling 2023 Qatar GP
"Since then, the track has removed some of the harshest edges of the kerbs, which resulted, alongside some cool conditions, teams attempting a one-stop strategy in the 2024 race.
"The difficulty with that was that even though the tyres were now not getting damaged, there was still lots of wear on the tyre because of the high-speed nature of the track. The tyre was wearing down on the surface more than Pirelli were happy with on those one-stop strategies which is why last year we had a 25-lap limit imposed and this year we have 27-lap limit."
How will it change how the teams prepare?
Bernie:"I think teams will have a heads up from Pirelli way before we found out, so they'll have had much longer to prepare for it.
"I think because it's not a Sprint weekend, teams have quite a good allocation of medium or hard tyres in order to do what they need to do. The problem with a Sprint weekend, which Qatar was last year, is that the 25-lap limit also applied through the Sprint itself and Qualifying as it's all cumulative through the weekend.
"So this year, with a normal weekend, and particularly with the medium tyres, the teams have loads available to play with.
Karun Chandhok was at the SkyPad to analyse whether McLaren's decision not to pit Oscar Piastri under the Safety Car on lap seven cost him the win at the 2025 Qatar GP
"So I'd expect the race to be similar to last year in terms of something like two sets of medium and one set of hard. They will probably still run a hard tyre in Practice Two to try it and then they'll save one for their race allocation. Some teams might save two for the race allocation.
"But I think with it not being a Sprint, the teams should have loads of tyres available to make it happen and it'll just depend on whether they think medium or hard is their preferred tyre for the race."
Bernie:"I don't think the 27-lap limit is very restrictive in terms of strategy because there is lots of freedom with the 57-lap race.
"The earliest you could stop and still do a two-stop race is lap three. So you'd do three laps on one tyre and then one stint of 27 laps followed by another of 27 laps. That strategy might be possible if there's a Safety Car early in the race, meaning you'd have to do one more stop to the end.

The Screens App Will Let You Turn Your iPhone Duo Into An Itty Bitty MacBook
The Screens app will let you turn your iPhone Duo into an itty bitty MacBook
The app’s latest update will turn half the display into a keyboard for tiny typing.
ByMariella MoonNov. 26, 2026 8:59 am ESTEdovia ScreensAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
Edovia's Screens is a remote desktop app, which gives you a way to control your computer for the iPhone, iPad, another Mac or even the Vision Pro. Screens 5.10.6, its latest update,adds the abilityto turn your iPhone Duointo a tiny MacBookwhen it's in a partially open, clamshell configuration. When the phone is folded halfway, you can use the app's new Laptop Mode to display your remote desktop on the upper half of the screen and a keyboard with trackpad below.
Its keyboard supports multiple languages, and you can swipe down on keys to see alternative characters like you can on the iPad. The trackpad supports Screens' gestures. Of course, they're not a complete replacement for actual physical keyboards and trackpads, but they could be good enough to use in a pinch, or even regularly if you're used to typing on a screen or don't need to type anything lengthy.
The iPhone Duo's form factor is so unlike previous iPhones that we'd love to see more fun ways developers can use it to create unique experiences for the device's users. Some developers, however, might not find it that easy: Instagram's Adam Mosserirecently saidthat it will be "pretty challenging" to design Instagram "in a way that feels great" for the device.

George Russell cools Max Verstappen feud by admitting: ‘It was quite amusing’
‘I don’t want to have poor relationships with people’
Dutchman said Mercedes driver was ‘below my level’
George Russell has insisted he has no interest in continuing his feud withMax Verstappen, describing it as avoidable and unnecessary, but also noting that he has no intention of backing down from comments he made at last week’s Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Russell and Verstappen, who have long endured a testy relationship, were once more at loggerheads atthe meeting in Nevada. Russell had called out the Dutchman after an incident where the pair clashed in practice, saying: “I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this.”
‘This isn’t F1’: Max Verstappen criticises overtake-heavy Las Vegas Grand PrixRead more
Verstappen went on to win in Las Vegas with a fine drive, while Russell, who had vied with him for much of the race, ended up in ninth after he locked up on the final laps. Verstappen gleefully welcomed the incident at the time and afterwards went on to dismiss the British driver as “below my level” and furthermore that he was: “nowhere near me. He’s been an absolute joke this season.”
Speaking before this weekend’s grand prix in Qatar, the penultimate race of the season, Russell maintained he would not be drawn into a further dispute with Verstappen, but also noted pointedly that he was not aiming to make friends with his competitors in F1.
“I want to win and it is as simple as that, it is not a war of words off track,” he said. “I don’t think it is important to have a good relationship, or no relationship with anyone. We are all competitors and there is no right or wrong way about the mentality that we all have.
“We are different and you don’t need to agree with one another. I am not looking to be best mates with anybody on the grid. But it is all avoidable and unnecessary and not something I am looking to continue. I don’t want to have poor relationships with people. That is not the type of person I am.”
View image in fullscreenRed Bull’s Max Verstappen ahead of George Russell during the Las Vegas Grand Prix.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA
Russell was asked repeatedly about what had happened and the exchanges between him and Verstappen, but took it in good humour and conceded Verstappen had the right to make the remarks because he had won the race.
“I found some of his comments after the race to be quite amusing,” Russell said. “At the end of the day, he drove an incredible race and won it and he can afford to say what he wants.
“I stand by what I said after practice, but he was the one that went out and won the race and I didn’t and I am sure he had a laugh about that.”
Verstappen has won four of the past six races and is second in the drivers’ championship with Russell having slumped to fourth, 40 points behind the Dutchman. The British driver admitted he had learned from the events of the previous week in that he felt he might have been too forthright with his opinions in the past.
“Maybe I have been guilty of being just too open and honest. I feel with all of the media and the journalists I have a good relationship with and you sometimes forget that you’re not talking to one person,” he said.
“I’m talking to millions of people on the television, so I think that good relationship has actually probably hindered me a little bit. That’s life lessons in this world we live in. The competition is on track and that’s where I want to have the battles. I respect Max immensely for his driving talents and everything he’s achieved on track. That’s that, really.”

Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid
November 26, 20264:44 AM ETHeard onMorning Edition
Puerto Rico Supreme Court allows governor to fire company that runs the island's troubled power gridListen·2:332:33TranscriptToggle more options
EmbedEmbed<iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-6054139/nx-s1-10020784" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player">
LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago. The court's ruling nullifies its contract, and gives the government a year to find a new operator.
Puerto Rico's supreme court has ruled the island's governor can kick out the private company that's been running its troubled power grid for five years. The decision could have huge consequences for electric service in Puerto Rico. Here is NPR's Adrian Florido.
ADRIAN FLORIDO, BYLINE: After Hurricane Maria flattened Puerto Rico's already rickety power grid in 2017, the island's government privatized it. It gave a company called LUMA Energy, based in Canada and Texas, a 15-year deal to take over the power lines, promising that LUMA would rebuild the grid stronger and improve the notoriously unreliable service. LUMA took over in 2021. But things have not gone as planned.
Blackouts are still a constant fact of life. LUMA has come in for harsh criticism from customers and officials. Last year, Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez-Colon filed suit to nullify LUMA's contract. Yesterday, the Puerto Rican Supreme Court ruled in her favor that LUMA must go.
JENNIFFER GONZALEZ-COLON: Today is a day of celebration on the island.
FLORIDO: This is the governor speaking after the ruling. She said LUMA has not lived up to its promises.
GONZALEZ-COLON: More outages on the island, more shutdowns on the island. They have not fulfilled the requirements of the contract.
FLORIDO: In fact, the island's supreme court ruled on procedural grounds, saying officials had not followed local requirements when approving agreements with the company. The court gave the local government a year to put a new operator in place. The governor said the work to find a new private company will start immediately.
GONZALEZ-COLON: It's going to be a good transition. We're going to make it in a year. And I hope that all companies that are interested in participating in this process will fulfill and follow the process of law. And we're going to be opening that process for public bid.
FLORIDO: The court gave LUMA Energy 10 days to request a reconsideration of its ruling. In a statement, LUMA said it is considering its legal options. The company has long argued that the grid it took over was in awful shape and that it is not fully to blame for the blackouts. A new operator will need approval from both the local government and a federal oversight board that Congress put in place 10 years ago to get Puerto Rico out of bankruptcy. In a statement, that board criticized the governor for ending LUMA' s contract without having a new company ready to go. It said it's worried about the continuity of service on the island. In her remarks yesterday, the governor said she has a plan in place and will reveal it soon.

‘No time for a culture war’: Victoria’s electricity supply is at risk. Can it avoid power shortages and bill shocks? | Victoria state election 2026 | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Yallourn power station, which provides about a fifth of Victoria’s energy, will be retired in mid-2028, leaving a narrow window to build replacement capacity.Photograph: Diego Fedele/AAPView image in fullscreenYallourn power station, which provides about a fifth of Victoria’s energy, will be retired in mid-2028, leaving a narrow window to build replacement capacity.Photograph: Diego Fedele/AAP
‘No time for a culture war’: Victoria’s electricity supply is at risk. Can it avoid power shortages and bill shocks?
State faces electricity supply gap when Yallourn coal-fired power station closes in 2028 as experts warn neither Labor nor the Coalition has adequate plans
Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here
Victoria’s electricity supply will be at risk when a major power plant shuts in 2028 and neither major party is offering a plan at this month’s state election to deal with it, experts have warned.
All parties concede the giant Yallourn coal plant, which has operated in the Latrobe Valley since the 1970s and supplies a fifth of Victoria’s energy, is at the end of its functional life and will shut in less than two years. Analysts say the parties vying to run the state are failing to properly explain how they will fill the power shortfall the closure will create.
The challenge facing Victoria is exacerbated by the growth in energy demand fromdatacentresand the electrification of buildings, homes and vehicles. Experts are most critical of the Coalition, under Liberal leader Jess Wilson, which is favoured to win the election. It says it would stop work on new transmission lines – the high-voltage power lines needed to connect new wind and solar farms and allow Victoria to import power from neighbouring states.
Tim Baxter, of consultancy Naru Research, says there is no “time for a culture war on energy in Victoria” because poor choices now would be “devastating” for the state’s economy and create bill shocks for households and businesses.
Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter
He says cheap gas helped build Victoria’s past prosperity, but it is quickly running out with offshore gas supply from Bass Strait in steep decline. And there isno evidencethe state has meaningful gas resources elsewhere to replace it. This has contributed to a 62% increase in gas prices in five years, he says, while electricity bills have risen by 18%.
Gas lobby ‘scare campaign’ urges Victoria to scrap ban in new homes, leaked documents showRead more
Given Victorians rely more on gas than other states, Baxter says it underlines the need for households to move away from gas and increasingly run on renewable energy. “Every windfarm, solar farm and battery that comes online before 2028 reduces how much expensive gas Victoria has to burn when Yallourn goes. That makes speeding up the build-out the single best way to protect households from higher bills,” he says.
What are Labor and the Coalition promising?
Victoria’s wholesale electricity prices are the lowest on the east coast, but households still rely heavily on expensive gas. Regardless of who wins, energy bills are likely to increase, according to a government briefingreportedin the Herald Sun.
The Coalition says it would scrap VNI West, a transmission line linking Victoria to New South Wales, and pause work on the Western Renewables Link, between Melbourne and the state’s west. Instead, it would undertake a “short, sharp and independent” review of the state’s transmission plan, which would consider alternatives, such as solar power on commercial and industrial rooftops.
It has also pledged to “throw open the doors to gas exploration”, reverse Labor’s policy of makingnew homes all-electric, and tender for new firming capacity with an Energy Security Requirement modelled on schemes in NSW and South Australia. There is no plan to change the state’s emission reduction targets – cutting greenhouse gas emissions by 75%–80% below 2005 levels by 2035 and reaching net zero emissions by 2045–but it has not said how it would achieve them.
Labor says it would continue to expand the power grid,shift homes from gas to electricity for heating and cookingand continue to support the development of offshore windfarms. But the Carroll government is also reviewing the Western Renewables Link. It recently cancelled a renewable energy zone, approved two gas developments (although one hassince entered administration), and announced $7.5m to kickstart a “renewable gasindustry”.
‘Time to put our foot on the accelerator’

Environment Victoria’s chief executive, Jono La Nauze, says the Coalition’s plan – including a proposal to reinstate a policy introduced by the previous Baillieu-Napthine Coalition government preventing wind turbines being built within 2km of dwellings – is “the greatest swindle ever attempted on Victorian voters”.

Court lets Puerto Rico governor fire firm that runs the island's troubled power grid
November 26, 20264:44 AM ETHeard onMorning Edition
Puerto Rico Supreme Court allows governor to fire company that runs the island's troubled power gridListen·2:332:33TranscriptToggle more options
LUMA Energy took over the electric grid five years ago.
Puerto Rico's supreme court has ruled the island's governor can kick out the private company that's been running its troubled power grid for five years.
The decision could have huge consequences for electric service in Puerto Rico.
ADRIAN FLORIDO, BYLINE: After Hurricane Maria flattened Puerto Rico's already rickety power grid in 2017, the island's government privatized it.

It gave a company called LUMA Energy, based in Canada and Texas, a 15-year deal to take over the power lines, promising that LUMA would rebuild the grid stronger and improve the notoriously unreliable service.
LUMA took over in 2021.
LUMA has come in for harsh criticism from customers and officials.
Last year, Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez-Colon filed suit to nullify LUMA's contract.
Yesterday, the Puerto Rican Supreme Court ruled in her favor that LUMA must go.
JENNIFFER GONZALEZ-COLON: Today is a day of celebration on the island.
FLORIDO: This is the governor speaking after the ruling.
She said LUMA has not lived up to its promises.
GONZALEZ-COLON: More outages on the island, more shutdowns on the island.
They have not fulfilled the requirements of the contract.
FLORIDO: In fact, the island's supreme court ruled on procedural grounds, saying officials had not followed local requirements when approving agreements with the company.
The court gave the local government a year to put a new operator in place.
The governor said the work to find a new private company will start immediately.
And I hope that all companies that are interested in participating in this process will fulfill and follow the process of law.
And we're going to be opening that process for public bid.
FLORIDO: The court gave LUMA Energy 10 days to request a reconsideration of its ruling.
In a statement, LUMA said it is considering its legal options.
The company has long argued that the grid it took over was in awful shape and that it is not fully to blame for the blackouts.
A new operator will need approval from both the local government and a federal oversight board that Congress put in place 10 years ago to get Puerto Rico out of bankruptcy.
In a statement, that board criticized the governor for ending LUMA' s contract without having a new company ready to go.
It said it's worried about the continuity of service on the island.
In her remarks yesterday, the governor said she has a plan in place and will reveal it soon.

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c39w:
Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility - BBC News
A Rheinmetall facility in Kuwait was targeted by Iran, Italian and Kuwaiti authorities said
Published26 November 2026, 15:36 GMT
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.
The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.
Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi saying "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by its military.
Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.
It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it hadrepelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces- the first strikes in more than two months on the country.
Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.
The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.
Meanwhile, Italy's foreign ministry said in a statement: "An explosion caused by a drone attack... occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working."
The two Italian nationals were working at an air defence detection station and performing maintenance work on systems used by the Kuwaiti Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa, citing Italy's foreign ministry.
Italian media outlets have named the two individuals. One of the men was reported to be 36, while the other was 65 and nearing retirement.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.
"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.
"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security issue for us all."

However, Iranian state media quotes the military saying there were no offensive or military operations in the region.
“Given the history of hostile actions and the role of the Zionist regime and American forces in using false flags and regional adventures, these accusations are considered a cover for continuing evil and an attempt to increase insecurity in the region,” said Iranian military spokesperson Sardar Shekarchi.
Italy’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation confirmed its citizens’ deaths, saying, “an explosion caused by a drone attack … occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working,” with Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani confirming the victims were technicians working at an air-defence surveillance station.
“Regarding the targeting of a vital site in the country as a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, the two injured Italian nationals have died as a result of their injuries,” said Kuwait’s Defence Ministry. It had earlier said the injured were taken to a hospital for treatment while the incident caused unspecified “material damage”.
Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi said the Iranian drone attack happened while the Kuwaiti National Guard and Kuwaiti military were meeting with an Italian delegation that was visiting, including the commander general of the Italian Carabinieri, Lieutenant-General Salvatore Lungo, as well as the Italian ambassador to Kuwait.
Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said she was informed of the “tragic deaths”.
“On behalf of myself and the Government, I express my deepest sorrow and extend my heartfelt condolences to the victims’ families,” Meloni wrote on X.
The countries of theGulf region“have in one voice said an attack against one is an attack against all and have continued to condemn these attacks as a violation of sovereignty”, but we’ve seen an uptick in attacks since September, said Basravi, reporting from Doha.
Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, secretary-general of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), strongly condemned Thursday’s “brutal” attack.
In a statement, Albudaiwi stressed that Iran’s continued attacks on Kuwait, targeting its vital facilities and endangering the lives of civilians, constitute a dangerous escalation and threaten regional security.
There was no immediate comment from Iran regarding the attack.
But it was in line with Tehran’s “policy change”, said Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar, reporting from the Iranian capital.
“Increasingly we have heard from the Iranian officials … saying that this state of no war, no peace cannot remain in place forever, and Iran is working on some military options … to break the status quo,” said Serdar.
The conflict– which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February – has seen the Gulf states caught in the crossfire, with US military facilities and energy installations on their soil targeted.
The United States and Iran are in a standoff over the vital Strait of Hormuz, with the US military working to escort ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Tehran’s attempts to close the strait.
Thursday’s deadly attack comes days after Kuwaitactivated its air defencesto counter drone strikes launched by Iran – the first since early September.

ByPeter Barabas&Euronews Doha bureauPublished on26 November 2026 - 14:19 GMT+1,Updated15:48ShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
Kuwait's military said four people were injured after "a number of hostile" Iranian drones were detected and intercepted in its airspace. Flights crossing Iraq toward the Gulf were given new headings ahead of Kuwait, shifting the international corridor.
Flights on the key air traffic corridor between Europe, the Gulf region and Asia crossing Iraq towards the Gulf were suddenly redirected south on Thursday afternoon amid reports that Kuwait’s airspace was closed.
The Kuwait military has since issued a statement that four people were injured after "a number of hostile" Iranian drones were detected and intercepted in its airspace.
"The Iranian aggression targeted a vital facility, causing falling shrapnel that injured four people," said a statement by the defence ministry, adding that the injured were taken to a hospital for treatment while the incident caused unspecified "material damage".
Two Italians working for German defence group Rheinmetall died, Italy's foreign ministry said.
Since the war in Iran broke out in late February, most international flights crossing Europe have been flying toward major hubs in Doha, Abu Dhabi, Dubai and other destinations via a route running through Turkey, Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and the UAE.
All flights on the corridor were given a new heading, prompting them to make a sharp turn ahead of Kuwait's airspace and move the entire international corridor toward neighbouring countries, including a flight on which Euronews reporters were travelling.

The drone attack on Kuwait comes just one day after the US Virtual Embassy in Iran said Tehran, Yemen's Houthis and other aligned groups may target US interests and citizens in the region, including companies and institutions.
Washington warned citizens across the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance after Iran attacked US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait and Yemen's Houthi forces struck a tower in Riyadh's financial district, wounding 11 people.
US citizens in the region were urged to monitor airline and airport operations and prepare for possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.

article.title: Các cuộc không kích của Israel tại Dải Gaza khiến nhiều người thiệt mạng, bao gồm quan chức Hamas
article.summary: Các đợt không kích mới đây của Israel tại Dải Gaza đã làm ít nhất tám người thiệt mạng, trong đó có một quan chức chính trị của Hamas và vợ ông, giữa lúc bạo lực tiếp diễn ở khu vực này.
body: Các cuộc không kích mới do Israel thực hiện tại Dải Gaza đã khiến ít nhất tám người thiệt mạng, bao gồm một quan chức chính trị cấp cao của Hamas cùng vợ của ông, theo các nguồn tin từ y tế và quan chức địa phương.

Vụ tấn công nhắm vào một căn hộ dân cư tại Deir al-Balah ở miền trung Gaza vào thời điểm rạng sáng đã cướp đi sinh mạng của Khaled Abu Nada, người giữ vai trò phó bộ trưởng giáo dục của Hamas, và người vợ Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada. Các đội cứu hộ và nhân viên y tế đã chuyển các thi thể đến Bệnh viện Al-Aqsa ở miền trung Gaza và Bệnh viện Al-Shifa ở thành phố Gaza.

Trong một tuyên bố chung, Thủ tướng và Bộ trưởng Quốc phòng Israel xác nhận chiến dịch này nằm trong chuỗi các cuộc nhắm mục tiêu vào giới chức Hamas. Thủ tướng Israel Benjamin Netanyahu cho biết khoảng 80 quan chức Hamas đã bị tiêu diệt trong tháng qua. Đồng thời, quân đội Israel tuyên bố sẽ tiếp tục theo đuổi các mục tiêu này nhằm bảo vệ an ninh.

Bên cạnh đó, các cuộc không kích khác tại khu vực phía đông Thành phố Gaza và trại tị nạn Shati cũng ghi nhận thêm nhiều thương vong. Các nguồn tin cho hay một số người làm việc cho lực lượng an ninh của Hamas đã thiệt mạng trong các đợt oanh tạc này. Những diễn biến quân sự này diễn ra trong bối cảnh bạo lực vẫn tiếp diễn tại Dải Gaza, nơi có khoảng 2,1 triệu người sinh sống, phần lớn là người phải di tản sau thời gian dài xung đột.

article.title: Những tính năng mới của Gemini AI trên Android Auto
article.summary: Google Assistant đang được thay thế bằng Gemini AI trên Android Auto, mang đến khả năng trò chuyện tự nhiên, tìm kiếm địa điểm thông minh, quản lý tin nhắn và điều khiển âm thanh nâng cao.
body: Google đang tiến hành thay thế trợ lý Google Assistant bằng hệ thống Gemini AI tiên tiến trên mọi nền tảng, bao gồm cả hệ thống điều khiển Android Auto trên ô tô. Khi tính năng này được kích hoạt trên màn hình xe, người dùng sẽ nhận biết thông qua biểu tượng ngôi sao nhỏ kèm theo hình sóng âm quen thuộc thay cho biểu tượng micro truyền thống.

Khác với phiên bản cũ, Gemini AI hoạt động như một đối tác hội thoại tự nhiên, có khả năng xử lý các truy vấn phức tạp và đa tầng từ người lái. Ví dụ, thay vì các lệnh đơn giản, người dùng có thể yêu cầu tìm kiếm các quán cà phê theo nhiều tiêu chí cụ thể cùng lúc và đặt các câu hỏi tiếp nối dựa trên ngữ cảnh xung quanh chuyến đi.

Trong quá trình di chuyển, hệ thống mới giúp tài xế xử lý tin nhắn và các tác vụ âm thanh mà không cần rời mắt khỏi mặt đường. Người dùng có thể yêu cầu đọc tin nhắn gần nhất từ các ứng dụng được hỗ trợ như Google Messages, WhatsApp hoặc yêu cầu tóm tắt các cuộc trò chuyện nhóm dài để nắm bắt nội dung nhanh chóng.

Bên cạnh các lệnh điều khiển nhạc, podcast hay sách nói quen thuộc, người dùng còn có thể hỏi trực tiếp về nghệ sĩ hoặc bài hát đang phát để tìm hiểu thêm thông tin chi tiết. Gemini cũng hỗ trợ cung cấp dự báo thời tiết chi tiết cho các điểm đến và giúp người dùng chuẩn bị ý tưởng hoặc tra cứu thông tin ngay trong lúc lái xe.

“Without prior warning, Israeli Apache helicopters fired two missiles directly and in succession at this residential apartment,” Al Jazeera’s Ashraf Abu Amra said, reporting from Deir el-Balah. Russian strikes kill seven in Ukraine as Kyiv hits three refineries | Euronews
BySerhiy Dubyna&Yulia Averyanova and Euronews RussianPublished on25 November 2026 - 15:06 GMT+1,Updated15:20ShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsappCopy/paste the article video embed link below:Copied
Russia's drone attack killed people in six Ukrainian regions and hit a Naftogaz gas production facility, a DTEK thermal power plant and power networks in several parts of the country. Ukrainian drones struck Russian refineries in Samara and Rostov regions and an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region.
Russia launched scores of drones at energy and civilian targets across Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, killing at least seven people in six regions, authorities said.
The attack involved 112 Shahed, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, of which 88 were shot down or neutralised, Ukraine's air force said.
One person was killed in Bila Tserkva in Kyiv region, where the strike damaged critical infrastructure, an Epicentr shopping centre and a Nova Poshta postal branch, local authorities said.
One person was killed and seven injured in Kharkiv region after a strike hit a minibus on a highway, regional governor Oleh Synehubov said. Two people aged 76 and 69 were killed and another wounded in Sumy region.
Two people were killed in Odesa region on Tuesday evening — a 41-year-old and a 17-year-old — and one person was killed and three wounded in Zhytomyr region. Casualties were also reported in Chernihiv and Donetsk regions.
Russian forces struck a Naftogaz gas production facility in the Poltava region, the acting head of the company Serhiy Fedorenko said.
A fire broke out and the facility suspended operations. "This is not the first such attack and, unfortunately, not the last," Fedorenko said, adding that Russia was deliberately targeting gas production "to deprive Ukrainians of heat in winter."
Energy facilities in the Dnipropetrovsk region were also hit, triggering emergency power cuts across several districts.
A significant number of consumers lost power in Zaporizhzhia region, Zaporizhzhyaoblenergo head Andriy Stasevskyi said. More than 9,000 customers were left without electricity in Odesa region following Tuesday evening's attacks, regional governor Oleh Kiper said.
The energy company DTEK reported a large-scale strike on one of its thermal power plants, causing serious damage and forcing it to stop generating electricity. DTEK did not specify the location, noting it was the third large-scale strike on its plants in November.
Ukraine strikes Russian refineries and airbase
Ukrainian drones simultaneously struck three Russian oil refineries overnight, hitting plants in Samara and Rostov regions, according to Ukrainian monitoring sources.
Two refineries in Samara region — the Kuibyshev and Syzran plants, both part of Rosneft — were struck, with fires breaking out at both facilities.
Regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed the attack but did not name the facilities, saying one person was killed, power had been cut in several districts and a number of schools would operate on an adjusted schedule.
Regional authorities said 145 drones were shot down over the Samara region. Euronews could not independently verify these claims.
The Syzran refinery has a processing capacity of 8.5 million tonnes of oil per year and produces petrol, diesel, aviation kerosene, fuel oil and bitumen.
The Kuibyshev refinery has a primary processing capacity of 8.8 million tonnes per year. Ukraine last struck the Syzran plant on 15 September. The Kuibyshev refinery was also struck that month.
The third refinery struck overnight was the Novoshakhtinsk plant in Rostov region. Regional governor Yuri Slyusar confirmed the attack, saying a combined strike of more than 50 drones and missiles lasted six hours before the plant suspended operations.
Russian oil refining volumes have fallen by an estimated 45% since late October, according to analysts.
Ukraine's General Staff also reported overnight strikes on the Savasleyka airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region, which it described as one of Russia's key aviation facilities and the base from which aircraft carrying Kinzhal missiles launch strikes on Ukrainian cities.
According to Kyiv's military, three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged and would be unable to fly "for some time".
Ukraine destroyed a span of the road section of the Crimean Bridge last week, halting car traffic, though train services have been restored.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strike was a response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, describing deep strikes inside Russia as "long-range sanctions".
Ukraine attacked the bulk carrier Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, claiming it transported military cargo. The following day it struck the Russian corvette Merkury in the Libyan port of Benghazi. Zelenskyy confirmed the warship had been sunk.
On Tuesday, Russia's Vladimir Putin threatened Ukraine with retaliation for its strikes on refineries and complained that Kyiv had not heeded calls from US President Donald Trump to halt attacks on oil processing facilities.
Zelenskyy had said Ukraine was prepared to stop striking Russian refineries only if Moscow halted its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza - BBC News
Dozens of Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in near daily air strikes over the past month
ByRushdi Abu AloufGaza correspondent,Reporting fromIstanbul
A Hamas political official and his wife were among eight Palestinians killed in three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday.
Local sources told the BBC a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah was targeted at dawn, killing Khaled Abu Nada - the deputy education minister - and his wife, Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada.
A Hamas Civil Defence spokesman said that rescue teams and medical personnel had transferred eight bodies to Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza and Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.
In a joint statement, Israel's prime minister and defence minister said the operation was "part of a series of targeted killings" against Hamas officials.
Thursday's strikes also reportedly killed three Palestinians on al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City. Their identities have not yet been established, eyewitnesses said.
In a separate strike on Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, three Palestinians working for Hamas's security services were killed. They were identified as Yasser al-Lahham, Iyad Ahmed and Ibrahim al-Mashal.
Image source,@netanyahu/XImage caption,
Khaled Abu Nada and his wife Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada were killed in the air strike
In a post X, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death of Khaled Abu Nada and said about 80 Hamas officials have been killed in the last month.
"No one in Hamas's leadership will succeed in evading us," he said, adding that the military would "continue to pursue our enemies and protect the security of Israeli civilians".
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had carried out a strike on a "senior" Hamas operative, and would provide further details later.
The attacks came a day after Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters were killed in Israeli air strike on their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City.
On Tuesday, the overall commander of Hamas's internal security service was among 10 Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes.
Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.
At least 1,705 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,772 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

Israel's defence minister on Thursday threatened to forcibly displace one million Palestinians in Gaza if Hamas does not move to voluntarily surrender its weapons, as previously promised.

The defence minister ofIsrael's interim government on Thursday made new threats to displace one million Palestinians in Gaza unlessHamasgives up its weapons, which the group had previously committed to do.
In a post on X, Israel Katz – who is known for his outspoken remarks – said that Hamas would either "disarm voluntarily" or the Israeli military "will disarm them as part of Operation Gideon's Chariots II – including another evacuation of one million Gaza residents southward".
This comes as three Israeli strikes overnight into Thursday killed eight Palestinians in Gaza City and Central Gaza, according to health officials at Shifa hospital and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital, where the casualties were taken.

Another two separate strikes in Gaza City killed three people each, according to the Shifa hospital.
Israel’s military said that one of the strikes targeted three militants without elaborating, and did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the other strike.
The overnight casualties are the latest in Gaza, where near-daily Israeli fire and airstrikes have persisted more than a year after aceasefiredeal was reached between Israel and Hamas.

Palestinian journalist killed by Israel in Gaza wins Rory Peck prize | War reporting | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Freelance journalist Mariam Dagga, 33, was renownn for her relentless reporting despite the personal losses she suffered throughout the Gaza war.Photograph: Jehad Alshrafi/APView image in fullscreenFreelance journalist Mariam Dagga, 33, was renownn for her relentless reporting despite the personal losses she suffered throughout the Gaza war.Photograph: Jehad Alshrafi/AP
Palestinian journalist killed by Israel in Gaza wins Rory Peck prize
Mariam Dagga shares award with two of her colleagues from AP for ‘powerful coverage’ of human cost of war
Mariam Dagga, the Palestinian war correspondent who was killed at the age of 33 in Gaza in an Israeli strike, has posthumously won the prestigious Rory Peck prize for freelance video journalists, the organisers announced on Wednesday.
She shares the award with two of her colleagues from the Associated Press (AP), Abdel Kareem Hana and Jehad Alshrafi, “for their powerful coverage of the human cost of the war” in the Palestinian territory, the Rory Peck Trust said.
Dagga, who has a teenage son named Ghaith, waskilled in August 2025 in an Israeli airstrike on a southern Gaza hospital, which claimed the lives of four other journalists.
The independent photographer and reporter had been working with the AP news agency since the beginning of the current conflict, triggered by Hamas’s 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.
Dagga was renowned for her relentless reporting despite the personal losses she suffered throughout the war. She filmed the death of a protester who was shot during the 2018 Great March of Return inGaza, when Israeli forces shot protesters marching towards the Gaza border fence, killing more than 220 people and wounding more than 9,200. She later discovered that the protester was her brother.
The war correspondent continued her work as a journalist during the war in Gaza over the last 22 months, working as a freelancer with the AP and Independent Arabia.
View image in fullscreenMariam Dagga’s father holds a camera and mobile phone belonging to his daughter after she was killed in August 2025.Photograph: Abdel Kareem Hana/AP
The AP’s executive editor, Julie Pace, said: “Journalists play an essential role in documenting events and informing the public, often at enormous personal risk.
“We honour Mariam and all journalists killed during this conflict and other conflicts – and remain committed to seeking answers about their deaths.”
French photographer Robin Tutenges was the recipient of the first Rory Peck award for photojournalism in recognition of his work on the conflict in Ethiopia’s northern Amhara region.
Sudanese freelance photographer and video journalist Ahmed Mohamed Abdalla, who works with Agence France-Presse, was shortlisted for the same award for his coverage of thefall of El Fasherto the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Sudan’s civil war.
Abdalla was not allowed to attend the prize-giving ceremony in London as the UK government refused to grant him a visa.
In a recorded video message shared during the ceremony, he told of how the capital of the North Darfur region’s besieged inhabitants had to eat livestock feed to survive amid the daily deluge of missiles.
The prize has been awarded since 1995 in memory of Northern Irish video journalist Rory Peck, who was killed in Moscow in 1993, to celebrate the work of freelance video journalists.

fact_units.text: Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza - BBC News
Dozens of Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in near daily air strikes over the past month
A Hamas political official and his wife were among eight Palestinians killed in three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday.
Local sources told the BBC a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah was targeted at dawn, killing Khaled Abu Nada - the deputy education minister - and his wife, Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada.
A Hamas Civil Defence spokesman said that rescue teams and medical personnel had transferred eight bodies to Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza and Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.
In a joint statement, Israel's prime minister and defence minister said the operation was "part of a series of targeted killings" against Hamas officials.
Thursday's strikes also reportedly killed three Palestinians on al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City.
Their identities have not yet been established, eyewitnesses said.
In a separate strike on Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, three Palestinians working for Hamas's security services were killed.
They were identified as Yasser al-Lahham, Iyad Ahmed and Ibrahim al-Mashal.
Khaled Abu Nada and his wife Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada were killed in the air strike
In a post X, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death of Khaled Abu Nada and said about 80 Hamas officials have been killed in the last month.
"No one in Hamas's leadership will succeed in evading us," he said, adding that the military would "continue to pursue our enemies and protect the security of Israeli civilians".
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had carried out a strike on a "senior" Hamas operative, and would provide further details later.

The attacks came a day after Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters were killed in Israeli air strike on their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City.
On Tuesday, the overall commander of Hamas's internal security service was among 10 Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes.
Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year.
Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.
At least 1,705 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,772 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

lead_title: Here’s Everything You Can Do With With the New Gemini AI on Android Auto

evidence_pages.https://www.wired.com/story/heres-everyt:
Here’s Everything You Can Do With With the New Gemini AI on Android Auto | WIREDSkip to main content
Google Assistant isbeing replaced by Google’s more advancedGemini AIacross all platforms, and that includes Android Auto. If the switch hasn’t happened yet on your own vehicle’s dashboard, then it should happen soon.
You’ll see a message onscreen announcing the arrival of Gemini, with the new “spark” icon (a small star by a sound-wave-like icon), instead of the traditional microphone when the AI is active.
If you've used Gemini before on your phone, on the web,or somewhere else, then you're going to know the extras that it brings over Google Assistant. It's a truly natural conversation partner that can dig deep into information available online, and respond to a much wider range of queries. Here's what the upgraded app can do specifically when you're traveling on the road.
Gemini can find places, and give you details about them.Courtesy of David Nield
All of the standard commands you might have already been using are still here, of course, like "navigate home" or “Where's the nearest Walmart?” With Gemini though, there's much more flexibility in what you can say without the AI getting confused or misunderstanding what you're asking about.
For example, your questions can be multilayered. Something like "find the nearest coffee shop that has a drive-thru and is open now" will look for those exact criteria. You're also able to ask context-sensitive follow-up questions, such as "What time will it shut?" or "How long will it take to get there?" if you need further details.
You can ask more general questions too, such as "tell me more about the place I'm heading to" or "Is there outdoor seating?” But bear in mind that Gemini will be limited to scouring the data on Google Maps for its information. (It's a disembodied AI that's never been anywhere.) If it doesn't know the answer to something, it should tell you that.
Overall, it's smarter in every aspect. I was recently navigating a difficult junction and couldn't work out whether the map was sending me left or right. I asked Gemini, "Will I be traveling east or west after the next turn?" and it figured out the answer. That helped me avoid veering off in the wrong direction.
Gemini can compose and summarize messages.Courtesy of David Nield
One of the major benefits of having a voice-controlled AI in the car is having it handle messaging and audio tasks without you needing to take your eyes off the road or fish around for a button. If you tell Gemini to “read my last message,” it'll speak it out for you and give you the opportunity to reply. You can also specify the app, otherwise Google Messages will be used by default—Google Chat and WhatsApp are among the others that are supported.
Gemini is able to give you summaries of group chats, which is really handy when you're on a drive and the conversations you're involved in are building up message after message that you can't check. Name a group chat in a supported app and ask for a summary, or just request summaries of unread messages. You'll be able to get the gist without checking each individual message.
The usual array of audio commands are here, carried over from Google Assistant, so you can quickly start or stop audio in your music, podcast, radio, and audiobook apps. As well as continuing from where you left off, you can also name artists, albums, and playlists that you want to queue up. YouTube Music and Spotify are among the apps supported, if you need to specify one.
Another extra from Gemini is being able to ask about the artist or song that's currently playing, and get more information on it. You might want to learn the history of a particular band, find out how long a certain song was at number one, or even get recommendations based on what's currently playing—just ask Gemini.
Ask anything you want about anything—including the weather.Courtesy of David Nield
Much more than Google Assistant, Gemini can help you learn something or develop some ideas while you're behind the wheel. If you're on the way to a movie premiere, you can ask Gemini about the history of the film, the director, and the actors, and it'll remember the context of your conversation. (It'll all get synced back to the Gemini app on your other devices.)
Voice commands such as “help me prepare for my interview” or “come up with ideas for a quick and easy meal to make for dinner" will initiate a chat with Gemini that you can continue throughout your journey—and hopefully arrive well-prepared or with dinner sorted (or whatever it is). Maybe don’t ask about anything too mind-bending, as you’ll still need to concentrate on driving.
Gemini will ask along the way for any information it needs about what you’re interviewing for or the ingredients you’ve got at home. You can also ask Gemini to quiz you on a certain topic or run a query on something you see on the journey—like a landmark or a restaurant you go past.
Finally, there’s always the weather: Gemini will give you forecasts for the areas and specific locations you give it, on whatever day you want within the next week or so. Perhaps more useful for journeys are questions like “When is the rain going to stop?” or “What are the weather conditions like at my destination?” which will help you plan your trip.

Wireless Android Auto Has A Phone Battery Draining Problem, But You Can Fix It
Wireless Android Auto has a phone battery draining problem, but you can fix it
A vent mount and a few settings changes are enough to block the drain.
ByLuke JamesNov. 24, 2026 11:45 am ESTRoman Vyshnikov/ShutterstockAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
An hour of wireless Android Auto can sap up to 16 percent of a phone's battery when you've got everything turned on. Navigation, as well as music, can heat your phone up, which isn't great news since most people will charge their phones during the drive. That charging adds even more heat, and a phone that gets too hot may slow down its own charging to protect the battery.
After all,wireless Android Auto uses both Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and both stay switched on for your entire drive. Long stints using navigation and other demanding apps while charging have been acknowledged as some of the reasons a Pixel can overheat. Once it's too hot, the phone might reduce processor performance or partly switch off mobile data, including 5G.
But there are a few things you can do to help mitigate battery drain and heat, like turning off 5G or using offline maps. And for longer drives, you can plug the phone in to maintain its charge and keep it out of direct sunlight, ideally near an air-conditioning vent to help it stay cool.
A USB cable can help keep your phone cooler than wireless charging
Google has said that managing heat was one of the main reasons it capped the Pixel 10 and Pixel 10 Pro at 15W wireless charging, because a wireless pad can add even more thermal energy. A phone that's sitting on a pad, which itself is probably on a sunny dashboard while running navigation, can build up heat from several sources at once, potentially slowing charging.
Google's advice to prevent a Pixel from overheating is to keep it out of direct sunlight and away from hot vehicles and poorly ventilated spots. One way to reduce heat is to use a vent mount while the vent is blowing cold air instead of a dashboard cradle in full sun. Even moving the phone somewhere with ample airflow while not relying on charging during wireless Android Auto use can help substantially.
A USB connection can generally keep your phone cooler and charge it more effectively than wireless Android Auto on a wireless charging mount. But car ports vary, and some vehicle USB ports could be too slow to stop the battery from draining, depending on automaker specifications. If you want to switch to a wired connection,Android Auto has a developer menu you can access in seconds. While Google removed the wireless Android Auto switch from the app's regular settings in version 8.7, it remains available in the hidden developer settings, so you can turn wireless Android Auto off and connect the phone with a USB cable.
Adjust these Android settings to reduce battery drain
Switching from 5G to LTE appears to make the biggest difference to battery life, because some networks force a phone to maintain an LTE connection alongside 5G, which increases power consumption. LTE is thankfully fast enough for navigation and music. Toimprove your Samsung Galaxy's battery performance, go toSettings>Connections>Mobile networks>Network modeand selectLTE preferred. On other phones, look for Network mode or Preferred network type. Turning off 3D buildings in Google Maps can also help to reduce heat. With your car parked, open Google Maps on the car's screen, go into itsSettingsand turn off3D buildings.
Google Maps can save a map of your route before you leave, reducing mobile data use and strain on the device. Tap your profile picture, thenOffline maps>Select your own map, adjust the area to cover your route and tapDownload. Offline maps can't reroute around live traffic or new road issues as they develop, so going offline is generally best saved for long, predictable drives such as those on a highway or where you're familiar with the roads.
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scanning help apps get better location information, too. You can switch both off underSettings>Location>Location services, removing another background job. Wireless Android Auto still needs Wi-Fi and Bluetooth turned on, though. To stop it launching when you don't want it to, you can toggle off the settingStart Android Auto while locked, which can prevent it from starting while your phone is locked. This doesn't stop calls from connecting over Bluetooth.

Energy bills will soar - here's how you can save energy to ease the pain - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,
Keeping yourself warm by wearing thick clothes, using blankets and having hot drinks can help reduce heating bills
ByKevin PeacheyCost of living correspondent
Energy billswill soar by 26% in the new yearas the war in Iran pushes up wholesale prices.
Typical household bills will rise by £37 per month as Ofgem's latest price cap comes into force from January to March, but experts say it is possible to keep rising bills in check.
Here are four areas to consider ahead of the increase.
Ofgem's price cap, as well as suppliers' fixed deals, set a limit on the price of each unit of energy, not the total bill.
So, you pay for what you use. Millions of people have cut back on their energy consumption during years of relatively high prices.
With the unit price of gas, in particular, set to soar, experts say you should take a fresh look at your energy use and renew good habits.
turning down the flow temperatureon a combi boiler - usually indicated by a radiator icon, to make it operate more efficiently
turning off the pre-heat facilityon some combi boilers, which would have kept some water heated up when not in use
turning down the thermostatone degree, although 18C is the recommended minimum
lowering radiator valvesoutside of the living room
turning off the heating before April
These are small changes but - alongside washing clothes at 30C, blocking draughts and batch cooking - they can reduce energy use and bills.
Ofgem says about five million people still pay their bill when it arrives every three months, rather than receive a monthly bill often initially based on an estimate.
Taking regular meter readings, or having a smart meter, while paying by monthly direct debit solves that problem.
Paying by direct debitcosts significantly less than by so-called standard credit - typically £138 cheaper a year.
Customers on prepayment schemes - usually people on low incomes struggling to pay bills - used to pay a higher rate than others, but now they pay slightly less than the capped direct debit variable rate.
Various deals may rely on paying by direct debit or having a smart meter.
3. Consider switching to a fixed rate
Moving to a fixed energy tariff means the price you are charged per unit of gas or electricity does not change every three months, although the total bill will still vary depending on how much energy you use.
The trouble is that it is very difficult to work out whether a fixed deal is a good deal at the moment, for those renewing fixed deals or looking for one for the first time.
Some fixed deals are available at unit prices below the next forecast price cap level. But should energy prices fall sharply then a longer-term fix might not seem such good value compared with the price cap.
So consumer group Which? also recommendspaying close attention to any exit feeswhen picking a fixed deal. If variable prices fall below your fixed rate and you want to get out of it before the end of your agreement period, you may have to pay a hefty sum.
Before you fix, consumer website MoneySavingExpert advises youlook at all the deals available, not just what your own supplier is offering.
4. Check what financial support you can get
The government will givea £100 paymentto millions of homes to help cover winter energy costs.It will go to homes in council tax bands A to Din England, with the equivalent expected in Scotland and Wales.
There are alsoa range of other forms of support specifically for people on low incomes.
This winter anyone on means-tested benefits will get £150 off their electricity bill.
Your supplier will apply the discount automatically unless you are in Scotland, where you will need to contact your energy company to ask for the help.
Some people will also be eligible for aCold Weather Payment,externaland most pensioners will receive the winter fuel payment.
Beyond that, most energy suppliers offer hardship grants for people struggling to pay their bills and the government'sFuel Direct Scheme,externalcan help you repay energy debt.
You can get more advice fromOfgem,external,Citizens Advice,external, or your own energy supplier. Trade body Energy UK hasa list of support schemes,external.
People on low incomes may also be eligible for grants to help with insulating their homes, and there are local schemes offering grants for solar panels, heat pumps and the like.
But if you are hunting around for grants, watch out for scams pretending to be official money-off schemes.
How is the cost of energy affecting your quality of life? What questions do you have?

‘You Can See Everything’ has made more than $100M worldwide | TechCrunch
1:42 PM PST · November 22, 2026Image Credits:Courtesy of A24
‘You Can See Everything’ has made more than $100M worldwide
“You Can See Everything,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’sdocumentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, reached an impressive box office milestone this weekend, becoming one of the few documentaries to make more than $100 million worldwide.
Variety reportsthat almost all of the film’s $102.4 million box office has come from U.S. audiences, from whom it has grossed $93.4 million so far.
“You Can See Everything” will be opening in many more countries over the next few months — starting with Mexico, Brazil, and Argentina on November 25 and 26 — so its box office total could end up significantly higher.
And while the documentary was alreadyan undeniable commercial successfor indie studio A24 (especially with a reported budget of $7 million), it could now surpass the records set by the highest-grossing documentaries of all time — “March of the Penguins” ($127 million globally) and “Fahrenheit 9/11” ($222 million globally).

Perhaps more useful for journeys are questions like “When is the rain going to stop?” or “What are the weather conditions like at my destination?” which will help you plan your trip.

Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life | TechCrunch
Image Credits:Cheng Xin / Getty ImagesAI
Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
Rebecca Bellan1:33 PM PST · November 24, 2026
AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. Butnew researchsuggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.
According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.
ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.
The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse,Dots, andClaude Duet, respectively.
In October, Meta said more than10 million peoplein the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implantsMuse directly into Instagram DMs. Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are.
ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems.
It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest-performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.
For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust.
Additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another task, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.
The findings highlight a major issue for users adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request.
While AI benchmarks have largely focused on coding, professional work, or testing on specific tasks, ShellBench is attempting to evaluate how models perform on multi-step personal tasks within different agent harnesses — the software that controls how a model accesses information, uses tools, and takes actions.
While the researchers found model choice had a greater overall impact on performance than harness choice, among the more capable models, AI agent performance became more dependent on the harness.
For example, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 when operating within the Pi harness, but it performed worse when both models were tested within Claude Code.
Meta’s Muse Wonder Full scored 56% in Pi, but only 38.1% in Claude Code. Meta’s Muse Wonder 1.0, meanwhile, averaged a success rate of 39.7% across the five harnesses tested.
Notably, while the researchers tested models from Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic, they didn’t evaluate them within the native harnesses of Muse, Dots, or Claude Duet, so the results may not be representative of the experience millions of consumers are having with the product today.
TechCrunch has reached out to Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and the researchers in the study.

evidence_pages.https://dantri.com.vn/o-to-xe-may/o-to-d:
Ô tô điện cỡ nhỏ Suzuki Ignis ra mắt, kích thước nằm giữa VF 3 và VF 5 | Báo Dân trí
Ô tô điện cỡ nhỏ Suzuki Ignis ra mắt, kích thước nằm giữa VF 3 và VF 5
(Dân trí) - Suzuki Ignis dự kiến mở bán tại châu Âu và các thị trường khác từ giữa năm sau, nhưng chưa có kế hoạch ra mắt Việt Nam.
Ngày 25/11, Suzuki chính thức ra mắt toàn cầu mẫu xe thuần điện Ignis. Đây là mẫu xe thuần điện cỡ nhỏ đầu tiên của hãng xe Nhật Bản, dự kiến mở bán tại châu Âu và các thị trường khác từ giữa năm sau.
Ignis vốn là mẫu hatchback sử dụng động cơ thuần xăng, với biến thể 3 cửa và 5 cửa, ra mắt thế hệ đầu tiên vào năm 2000. Đến năm 2016, xe bước sang thế hệ thứ hai với nhiều nâng cấp đáng kể, bao gồm bổ sung tùy chọn hệ truyền động hybrid.
Suzuki Ignis thế hệ thứ ba chuyển sang sử dụng hệ truyền động thuần điện (Ảnh: Suzuki).
Phiên bản vừa ra mắt thuộc thế hệ thứ ba, và chỉ còn duy nhất tùy chọn hệ truyền động thuần điện. Tuy nhiên, Ignis thế hệ thứ ba thực chất là phiên bản quốc tế của Suzuki eSky, một mẫu kei-car dành cho thị trường nội địa Nhật Bản.
Cụ thể, xe trang bị cụm truyền động eAxle nhỏ gọn đặt ở cầu trước, tích hợp mô-tơ điện, bộ biến tần và hộp số giảm tốc thành một khối duy nhất, cho công suất tối đa 90 mã lực và mô-men xoắn 133Nm.
Pin LFP có dung lượng 26kWh. Các tùy chọn sạc bao gồm sạc chậm AC 7,4kW và sạc nhanh DC 50kW.Thời gian sạc và tầm vận hành mỗi lần sạc đầy chưa được hãng xe Nhật công bố.
Thế hệ thứ ba của Suzuki Ignis được phát triển trên nền tảng EV chuyên dụng có tên HEARTECT-e với khu vực dưới thân xe được tối ưu để chứa pin. Hệ thống treo cũng được tinh chỉnh, cùng bán kính vòng quay tối thiểu 4,5m.
Ignis thế hệ thứ ba vẫn giữ lối thiết kế hình hộp đặc trưng từ thế hệ trước, nhằm tối ưu không gian khoang cabin. Mặt ca lăng phía trước sơn đen bóng, nằm giữa cụm đèn pha LED cùng dải đèn định vị ban ngày hình chữ C. Mâm xe kích thước 15inch với phía trước dùng phanh đĩa, và phía sau dùng phanh tang trống.
Xe sở hữu kích thước dài x rộng x cao lần lượt 3.570 x 1.565 x 1.635mm, cùng chiều dài cơ sở 2.460mm, khoảng sáng gầm 150mm. Khoang cabin có bốn chỗ ngồi.
Kích thước này tương đương dòng hatchback hạng A Kia Morning (chiều dài 3.595mm và chiều dài cơ sở 2.400mm). Nếu so với xe thuần điện, Ignis sẽ nằm giữaVinFastVF 3 và VF 5 về kích thước.
Dù sử dụng hệ truyền động thuần điện, nhưng khoang cabin vẫn mang nhiều dấu ấn của xe động cơ đốt trong. Các khu vực điều khiển có bố cục rõ ràng, không tích hợp hầu hết tính năng vào màn hình trung tâm.
Qua hình ảnh, có thể thấy xe dùng cụm đồng hồ dạng điện tử, vô lăng tích hợp nút bấm, cần số đặt cao, phanh tay điện tử và ghế bọc chất liệu nỉ.
Phía Suzuki Việt Nam cho biết, Ignis mới hiện chưa có kế hoạch phân phối tại thị trường Việt Nam.
Ở thời điểm hiện tại, dải sản phẩm của hãng có 3/4 mẫu xe trang bị động cơ mild hybrid (MHEV), bao gồm Swift, Fronx và XL7. Chỉ còn duy nhất Jimny sử dụng động cơ thuần xăng.
Ở Việt Nam, hybrid vẫn là hướng đi phù hợp với các thương hiệu Nhật Bản nhờ có sẵn lợi thế về uy tín, độ bền và công nghệ đã được chứng minh hiệu quả. Bằng chứng là dải sản phẩm xăng lai điện của Toyota, Honda hay Suzuki đều đang ghi nhận sức mua tốt.
Đối với mảng xe thuần điện, các thương hiệu Nhật Bản vẫn tỏ ra thận trọng do áp lực cạnh tranh về giá bán, công nghệ cũng như hạ tầng trạm sạc.
Suzuki XL7 2026 sắp mở bán có thể được chốt giá khởi điểm hấp dẫn hơn
Với một số trang bị hướng tới việc tối ưu chi phí, phiên bản tiêu chuẩn của Suzuki XL7 2026 sắp ra mắt được kỳ vọng sẽ có mức giá thấp hơn trước đây.
Các hãng ô tô tăng ưu đãi, cạnh tranh doanh số cuối năm
Trong tháng 11, Mitsubishi bổ sung ưu đãi cho Xpander và Xforce, trong khi nhiều mẫu xe cùng phân khúc như Toyota Veloz Cross, Suzuki XL7, Hyundai Creta và Mazda CX-5 cũng được giảm giá mạnh.
Loạt ô tô Nhật Bản có thể về Việt Nam thời gian tới
Thị trường ô tô Việt Nam dự kiến đón nhiều mẫu xe đáng chú ý, như Honda Avancier, Toyota Innova Cross, Fortuner phiên bản nâng cấp và Pajero thế hệ mới.
Mitsubishi Outlander thế hệ mới chốt ngày ra mắt tại Việt Nam
Mitsubishi Motors Việt Nam xác nhận Outlander thế hệ mới sẽ ra mắt ngày 11/12, sau khi những lô xe đầu tiên cập cảng. Mẫu SUV cỡ C được nhập khẩu từ Nhật Bản, sử dụng hệ truyền động hybrid nhẹ 48V.

Xe có 34 giường, sử dụng pin 357 kWh, phạm vi di chuyển khoảng 450 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy.
Sáng 21.11, Công ty cổ phần Xe khách Phương Trang (FUTA Bus Lines) chính thức công bố đưa 100 xe giường nằm thuần điện KIMLONG99 EV-G34 vào khai thác vận tải hành khách liên tỉnh. Đây là dòng xe doKim Long Motornghiên cứu, sản xuất tại Việt Nam với cấu hình 34 giường đầy đủ tiện nghi.
Dàn xe giường nằm thuần điện KIMLONG99 EV-G34 có mặt tại Bến xe Miền Tây, TP.HCM
Trước đó, Kim Long Motor đã bàn giao lô xe này cho Phương Trang vào ngày 23.10.2026. Trong giai đoạn đầu khai thác, loại xe này sẽ hoạt động trên ba tuyến TP.HCM - Đà Lạt; TP.HCM - Cần Thơ và TP.HCM - Trà Ôn (thuộc Vĩnh Long).
Xe giường nằm điện chạy hơn 400 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy
Nhìn từ bên ngoài, KIMLONG99 EV-G34 khác biệt không quá nhiều so ới các dòng xe giường nằm khác trên thị trường Việt Nam hiện nay. Tuy nhiên, điểm đặc biệt ở chỗ mẫu xe này không phát ra tiếng ồn, không sử dụng động cơ dầu diesel và không có ống xả khí thải - một trong những nguyên nhân gây ô nhiễm môi trường.
KIMLONG99 EV-G34 sử dụng pin của BYD và mô-tơ điện, phạm vi hoạt động 450 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy
Mẫu xe giường nằm này sử dụngmô-tơ điệnvà bộ pin BYD, dung lượng 357 kWh, có thể di chuyển quãng đường 450 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy. Nhà sản xuất trang bị cho KIMLONG99 EV-G34 hai cổng sạc chuẩn CCS2, tương thích trụ sạc nhanh DC 240 kW, giúp sạc đầy pin trong khoảng 90 phút.
Ngoài ra, khoang hành khách bố trí 34 giường, mỗi giường có rèm che riêng tư, cửa gió điều hòa và nút gọi hỗ trợ. Xe trang bị tủ lạnh, hệ thống giải trí; các công nghệ an toàn gồm ABS, kiểm soát lực kéo ASR, phanh tái sinh và quản lý nhiệt pin.
Đối với xe khách đường dài, thời gian sạc và vị trí trạm sạc là những yếu tố ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến lịch trình di chuyển. Để giải bài toán này, hạ tầng trạm sạc FUTA EV Power sẽ được quy hoạch dọc các tuyến đường huyết mạch, trạm dừng chân và bến xe trên toàn quốc.
Khu vực điều khiển xe KIMLONG99 EV-G34 khá gọn nhưng đầy đủ chức năng điều khiển
Ông Phan Văn Hải - Tổng Giám đốc FUTA Bus Lines, cho biết: "Chúng tôi nhận thức rằng đưa xe điện vào khai thác trên các tuyến liên tỉnh đòi hỏi sự chuẩn bị đồng bộ trong quá trình tổ chức hạ tầng trạm sạc, công tác bảo dưỡng kỹ thuật đến đào tạo đội ngũ nhân sự". Doanh nghiệp sẽ tiếp tục giám sát kỹ thuật, tiếp nhận phản hồi hành khách để hoàn thiện dịch vụ.
Kim Long Motor hướng đến nội địa hóa 90%
Việc đưa 100 xe giường nằm thuần điện vào hoạt động đánh dấu bước mở rộng của Phương Trang từ vận tải công cộng đô thị sang vận tải hành khách đường dài. Hiện nay, FUTA Bus Lines đã phối hợp với Kim Long Motor triển khai hơn 1.500 xe buýt thuần điện hoạt động tại TP.HCM và Đà Nẵng.
Xe bố trí 34 giường với nhiều tiện nghi, có rèm che, điều hòa độc lập, cổng sạc...
Phương Trang cũng công bố triển khai chuyển đổi phương tiện xe buýt đô thị thuần điện tại Cần Thơ và Đà Lạt từ 20.11, đồng thời tiếp tục đầu tư trạm sạc, công nghệ pin và nguồn lực kỹ thuật để phục vụ đội xe ngày càng mở rộng.
Trong khi đó, Kim Long Motor đặt mục tiêu từng bước làm chủ công nghệ, linh kiện và chuỗi cung ứng. Khi bàn giao KIMLONG99 EV-G34, doanh nghiệp công bố tỷ lệ nội địa hóa của sản phẩm đạt 60%, đồng thời hướng đến mức 90% vào cuối năm 2026.
Ông Đào Viết Ánh - Tổng Giám đốc Kim Long Motor đặt mục tiêu đạt 90% tỉ lệ nội địa hóa vào cuối năm 2026 với dòng xe KIMLONG99 EV-G34
Ông Đào Viết Ánh - Tổng Giám đốc Kim Long Motor nhấn mạnh: "KIMLONG99 EV-G34 là sản phẩm được nghiên cứu, phát triển và sản xuất tại Khu công nghiệp sản xuất ô tô KIM LONG MOTOR Huế với mục tiêu đạt tỷ lệ nội địa hóa 90% vào cuối năm 2026".
Kim Long Motor đang phát triển tổ hợp công nghiệp ô tô tại Huế, diện tích quy hoạch giai đoạn một hơn 600 ha. Doanh nghiệp hướng đến làm chủ các công đoạn đúc, dập, gia công, sản xuất linh kiện, phụ tùng, lắp ráp và hoàn thiện, qua đó tăng tỉ lệ nội địa hóa.
Kim Long Motor tung 3 mẫu xe tải mới ra thị trường, giá từ 349 triệu đồng
Kim Long Motor vừa khánh thành nhà máy sản xuất ô tô tại Huế và tung ra 3 mẫu xe tải mới, theo định hướng lấy mảng xe tải làm chủ lực. Sự kiện này đánh dấu bước đi quan trọng trong việc xây dựng hệ sinh thái sản xuất ô tô nội địa tại Việt Nam.
