fact_units.text: Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM kỷ niệm 45 năm thành lập, trao 99 giải ảnh quốc tế - Tuổi Trẻ OnlineBỏ qua đến nội dung chính
Đăng ký Tuổi Trẻ SaoVào trang Tuổi Trẻ Sao
Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM kỷ niệm 45 năm thành lập, trao 99 giải ảnh quốc tế
và 1 tác giả khácHOÀI PHƯƠNGVĂN TRUNG
Hơn 4.300 ảnh từ 38 quốc gia, vùng lãnh thổ hội tụ tại Cuộc thi ảnh nghệ thuật quốc tế TP.HCM lần thứ 4.
Nhân kỷ niệm 45 năm thành lập, Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM trao 99 giải cho các tác phẩm xuất sắc.
Ghi nhận sự đóng góp của các nhiếp ảnh gia cho Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM - Ảnh: VĂN TRUNG
Tối 22-11,Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCMtổ chức lễ kỷ niệm 45 năm thành lập, tại công viên Lê Văn Tám (phường Tân Định, TP.HCM).
Đồng thời, ban tổ chức trao giảiCuộc thi ảnh nghệ thuật quốc tế TP.HCMlần thứ 4 vàLiên hoan Ảnh nghệ thuật truyền thốnglần thứ 51.
Cuộc thi ảnh quốc tế thu hút tác giả từ 38 quốc gia

ÔngĐoàn Hoài Trung- Chủ tịch Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM, ôn lại chặng hành trình xây dựng và phát triển của hội trong 45 năm qua, đồng thời ghi nhận những đóng góp của các thế hệ hội viên đối với phong trào nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM.

Một trong những hoạt động nổi bật được Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM tổ chức trong năm 2026 làCuộc thi ảnh nghệ thuật quốc tế TP.HCMlần thứ 4, với sự bảo trợ của Liên đoàn Nghệ thuật Nhiếp ảnh quốc tế (FIAP), Hội Nhiếp ảnh Hoa Kỳ (PSA) và Hội Nghệ sĩ nhiếp ảnh Việt Nam (VAPA).
Cuộc thi ảnh Nghệ thuật Quốc tế trao 107 giải thưởng, không nhận ảnh AI
Ban tổ chức nhận được 4.310 ảnh của 411 tác giả đến từ 38 quốc gia, vùng lãnh thổ.
Trong đó có 1.292 ảnh màu, 1.061 ảnh đen trắng, 1.013 ảnh chân dung và 944 ảnh hành động.
Chủ tịch Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM cho biết ảnh dự thi được ban giám khảo gồm những nhànhiếp ảnhuy tín trên thế giới chấm công tâm, trách nhiệm.
Cuộc thi có 99 tác phẩm đoạt giải và một giải Huy chương xanh FIAP.
Dịp này, Hội Nhiếp ảnh TP.HCM cũng trao giảiLiên hoan Ảnh nghệ thuật truyền thốnglần thứ 51.
Đáng chú ý, giải thưởng ảnh đen trắng mang tên cố nghệ sĩ nhiếp ảnhLâm Tấn Tàinăm nay được trao kèm huy chương cùng tiền thưởng.
Ban tổ chức trao giải thưởng cho các nhiếp ảnh gia - Ảnh: VĂN TRUNG
Gắn kết nhiếp ảnh quốc tế với sáng tác tại TP.HCM

Trong khuôn khổLễ hội Nhiếp ảnh Quốc tế TP.HCM 2026, trại sáng tác nhiếp ảnh quốc tếTP.HCM - Thành phố Nhiếp ảnhquy tụ 38nhiếp ảnh gia quốc tếđến từ 15 quốc gia, vùng lãnh thổ và hơn 60 nhiếp ảnh gia Việt Nam từ nhiều tỉnh, thành.

Các nghệ sĩ nhiếp ảnh quốc tế đến từ Anh, Nhật Bản, Hàn Quốc, Úc, Singapore, Brunei, Ba Lan, Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ, Pakistan, Nga, Bỉ… Cuộc thi tạo cơ hội cho nhiếp ảnh gia trực tiếp khám phá, trải nghiệm và thể hiện tình yêu thành phố qua ống kính.

Thông qua các hoạt động sáng tác, giao lưu và trao giải, chương trình góp phần kết nối các nhiếp ảnh gia trong nước và quốc tế, đồng thời tạo dịp để giới nhiếp ảnh gặp gỡ, chia sẻ kinh nghiệm và giới thiệu những tác phẩm nghệ thuật.
Trình diễn áo ngũ thân trong khuôn khổ lễ kỷ niệm - Ảnh: VĂN TRUNG
Lễ hội Nhiếp ảnh Quốc tế TP.HCM 2026 mang đến nhiều triển lãm, hoạt động sáng tác và giao lưu dành cho người yêu nhiếp ảnh - Ảnh: VĂN TRUNG

article.title: Mauricio Pochettino ra mắt Manchester United trong chuyến làm khách đầy thử thách tại Anfield
article.summary: Mauricio Pochettino chính thức bắt đầu hành trình dẫn dắt Manchester United bằng trận đấu quan trọng với đối thủ truyền kiếp Liverpool tại Anfield, trong bối cảnh đội bóng đang gặp nhiều khó khăn tại Premier League.
body: Mauricio Pochettino đã chính thức bắt đầu nhiệm kỳ huấn luyện viên trưởng tại Manchester United bằng một thử thách lớn: chuyến làm khách đến sân Anfield để đối đầu với đối thủ truyền kiếp Liverpool. Đây là trận đấu đánh dấu sự trở lại của chiến lược gia người Argentina tại Premier League, sau khi ông rời vị trí dẫn dắt đội tuyển quốc gia Mỹ. Pochettino tiếp quản 'Quỷ đỏ' trong bối cảnh đội bóng đang trải qua giai đoạn khủng hoảng phong độ, hiện xếp thứ 19 trên bảng xếp hạng với chỉ 8 điểm sau 10 vòng đấu đầu tiên.

Trước trận đấu này, Manchester United đã trải qua sự thay đổi nhân sự trên băng ghế huấn luyện sau khi Michael Carrick rời đi. Pochettino bắt đầu công việc mới từ thứ Năm, đồng nghĩa với việc ông có rất ít thời gian để chuẩn bị cho cuộc đối đầu tại Anfield. Trong khi đó, Liverpool đang đứng thứ năm và đặt mục tiêu giành chiến thắng để thu hẹp khoảng cách với đội đầu bảng Arsenal, sau khi đối thủ này bị Newcastle cầm hòa 2-2 vào thứ Bảy.

Sự kiện này cũng thu hút sự chú ý lớn từ dư luận sau khi những hình ảnh về buổi tập đầu tiên của Pochettino bị rò rỉ qua thiết bị bay không người lái (drone). Pochettino đã lên tiếng bày tỏ sự không hài lòng về hành động này, cho rằng việc quay lén các buổi tập kín là không phù hợp và tiềm ẩn nhiều rủi ro. Dù câu lạc bộ chưa có kế hoạch khởi kiện, vấn đề an ninh tại trung tâm huấn luyện Carrington đã trở thành chủ đề được quan tâm trước thềm trận đấu.

Bên cạnh áp lực từ kết quả thi đấu, tương lai của đội trưởng Bruno Fernandes cũng là tâm điểm. Tiền vệ người Bồ Đào Nha xác nhận rằng các cuộc đàm phán gia hạn hợp đồng hiện đang bị tạm hoãn để tập trung giải quyết những khó khăn của đội bóng trên sân cỏ. Với việc Pochettino khẳng định sẽ trực tiếp đưa ra các quyết định về đội hình, người hâm mộ đang chờ đợi sự thay đổi trong cách vận hành chiến thuật của Manchester United dưới thời tân huấn luyện viên.

article.title: Tom Jackson, huyền thoại NFL và gương mặt biểu tượng của ESPN, qua đời ở tuổi 75
article.summary: Tom Jackson, cựu hậu vệ xuất sắc của Denver Broncos và nhà phân tích thể thao kỳ cựu tại ESPN, đã qua đời ở tuổi 75, để lại niềm tiếc thương sâu sắc trong cộng đồng bóng bầu dục Mỹ.
body: Thế giới bóng bầu dục Mỹ vừa đón nhận tin buồn khi Tom Jackson, cựu hậu vệ huyền thoại của đội Denver Broncos và gương mặt quen thuộc trên sóng ESPN, đã qua đời ở tuổi 75. Sự ra đi của ông được chính nhà đài ESPN xác nhận, để lại niềm tiếc thương vô hạn cho đồng nghiệp, người hâm mộ và các thế hệ cầu thủ.

Trước khi trở thành một nhà phân tích truyền hình nổi tiếng, Tom Jackson đã có một sự nghiệp thi đấu lẫy lừng. Được Denver Broncos lựa chọn ở vòng bốn của kỳ tuyển chọn NFL Draft năm 1973 từ Đại học Louisville, ông đã cống hiến trọn vẹn 13 năm thi đấu chuyên nghiệp cho đội bóng này. Jackson là trụ cột không thể thay thế trong hàng phòng ngự "Orange Crush" trứ danh, từng ba lần góp mặt trong trận đấu Pro Bowl và được vinh danh tại Ring of Fame của câu lạc bộ.

Sau khi giải nghệ vào năm 1987, Jackson bắt đầu chương hai đầy rực rỡ trong sự nghiệp tại ESPN. Ông trở thành mảnh ghép hoàn hảo bên cạnh Chris Berman trong các chương trình ăn khách như "NFL Primetime" và "Sunday NFL Countdown" suốt gần ba thập kỷ. Sự kết hợp giữa Jackson và Berman không chỉ mang lại kiến thức chuyên môn sâu sắc mà còn tạo nên sự gắn kết, hài hước, giúp nâng tầm các chương trình studio về bóng bầu dục trở thành biểu tượng văn hóa thể thao.

Sự kính trọng dành cho Tom Jackson được thể hiện rõ qua những lời tri ân từ khắp nơi. Chris Berman, người bạn đồng hành lâu năm, đã gọi ông là "một trong những con người tuyệt vời nhất từng bước đi trên hành tinh này". Trong khi đó, Ủy viên NFL Roger Goodell ca ngợi Jackson là người đã mang đến sự uy tín, niềm đam mê và sự chân thành vào mọi công việc ông làm. Để ghi nhận những đóng góp to lớn, ESPN thậm chí đã đặt tên studio bóng bầu dục của mình theo tên của bộ đôi Chris Berman và Tom Jackson.

Sự ra đi của Tom Jackson không chỉ là mất mát của một cựu cầu thủ hay một bình luận viên, mà là sự chia tay với một nhân vật đã kết nối nhiều thế hệ người hâm mộ với môn thể thao này. Di sản của ông, từ những pha cản phá trên sân cỏ đến những phân tích sắc sảo trên truyền hình, sẽ còn được ghi nhớ mãi.

4 Random Apps You Might Not Realize Work With Android Auto
4 random apps you might not realize work with Android Auto
Some of these apps will be familiar, while others you may not have heard of.
ByGabriela VătuNov. 22, 2026 11:15 am ESTGabriela Vatu for EngadgetAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
Android Auto users typically utilize just a few basic apps like Google Maps for directions and Spotify for music. They don'tdive into the developer menu; they don't make any serious changes to the way Android Auto works; and they don't know they could be spending all those minutes waiting for someone in a parking lotplaying games directly on the car's infotainment display. But the platform's compatible app library runs much deeper, well beyond navigation and streaming.
Android Auto actually supports a surprising range of communication and meeting tools, like WhatsApp and Google Meet, and even a bunch of other apps to help you navigate more efficiently. Each one adds layer after layer of functionality that most users never think to explore. Discovering new apps can genuinely change how you commute while also making it possible to enjoy your drive just a tiny bit more.
Take your work on the road with Google Meet
Android Auto comes with some extra functionality for those in the corporate world, as several popular apps come with Android Auto support for meetings and calls, with Google Meet leading the way. Because Meet is Google's own app, it fits naturally into the Android Auto experience. You can see your upcoming meetings on the car display and join a call with a single tap, all in audio-only mode so your eyes stay on the road. Whether it's a short check-in with your manager or a longer team call, Meet makes it easy to keep up with your schedule even if you have to drive around.
Google's app isn't the only option, though. Zoom, Webex by Cisco and Microsoft Teams all work on Android Auto, offering users the opportunity to join video conferences with audio only. Some apps take integration a step further. Microsoft Teams, for instance, lets users check their calendar and place calls directly from the car display. Google Meet also displays upcoming meetings on your schedule. These features are particularly useful if you're often traveling from location to location but still have to participate in meetings along the way. They also help if you have to leave early to pick up the kids from school while a meeting is still on your calendar.
One thing to mention about these apps is that, depending on your employer, restrictions may apply. Certain companies require corporate apps like Google Meet and Microsoft Teams to run inside an isolated Android Work Profile. In such situations, Android Auto may block calendar sync or prevent the app from appearing on the screen. There's aWork Mode in the works on Android Auto, though, so it may soon be easier to reach all those apps that are locked out by your employer.
With gas prices being what they are these days, it's more important than ever to know where to fuel up. Apps likeFueliocan help with that when you're looking for a place to put gas in your car without breaking the bank. Fuelio tracks fill-ups, odometer readings and fuel prices, then calculates your average fuel economy and cost per mile over time. You can even use various filters to display gas stations that were updated within the past day, or those that are most appreciated by users.
Google Maps and other similar tools can surface the nearest gas stations and even tell you the latest prices, but Fuelio gives more in-depth information regarding fuel type, distance and more. Plus, when you throw in all the other features, it's a much better fit if you want to know exactly how much your car is costing you. While Fuelio is free to use with Android Auto, there is a premium version available that costs money.
If you're driving an EV, then the app you absolutely must use through Android Auto isPlugShare. This free tool (the paid version removes ads) gives you access to a crowd-sourced map that lets you see the nearest charging stations along your route. Its real strength is the community behind it, because drivers leave real-time feedback, uploading photos of the charger layout, reporting broken plugs and checking in after charging. That gives you a clear picture of what to expect before you pull in, so a station that looks fine on paper but has been out of service for days won't catch you off guard.
There are loads of filters you can play with, letting you choose the exact plug type, charging speed and network. You can also check which amenities are nearby, such as restrooms or a place to grab coffee while you wait. It's also a great tool for long-distance drives, as it automatically recommends charging stops along the way based on your specific EV model's range. That goes a long way toward easing the range anxiety that comes with getting an electric car. The one downside is that the data is only as good as its contributors, so stations in less-traveled areas may have fewer recent reports.
Go offline without losing your way with HERE WeGo
Data can be expensive, especially if you use your phone a ton. When you're traveling abroad, costs go up by quite a bit, so you should make the most of your home Wi-Fi. Apps likeHERE WeGothrough Android Auto offer offline navigation, so your data plan isn't ever a concern. HERE WeGo lets you download maps for entire countries so you always know where you're going. For some countries, you can download maps for certain areas, such as for Germany where you can grab a map for Berlin and another for Hamburg. In the United States, you can grab maps for entire states, but not separate cities.
There are plenty of features to fiddle with to make this app yours, like choosing which fuel type your car uses, having the metric vs. imperial system displayed the way you prefer and so on. The app will flag parking spots and rest areas along the route, and you can even tell it what types of things to avoid. For instance, Waze lets you avoid ferries and highways, but HERE WeGo can have you avoid tunnels and U-turns too. The app can take things one step further and even use visual references on route, which means it will tell you to make a right at the traffic light or when you reach a certain landmark.

Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment
Hotly anticipated Bonnie and Clyde-inspired adventure GTA VI has gamers glued to their screens around the world
Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to vicariously embark on police chases and coordinate robberies as the latest instalment of the eagerly anticipated series arrived.
GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired crime adventure game set in the fictional US state of Leonida, was launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13-year wait.
The hype around the release led to schools encouraging pupils not to miss lessons in anticipation of “GTA flu”, a term coined for the swathe of absences when GTA V was released in 2013, which is expected to recur over the coming weeks. The human resources platform Remote said there had been a 32% increase in leave requests worldwide on Thursday.
Birchgrove comprehensive school in Swansea, south Wales, had warned parents and carers that despite the “considerable excitement”, studies should remain a priority.
Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love storyRead more
The Sandon secondary school in Essex entered students into a raffle for £10 Amazon vouchers, a lunchtime queue-jump pass and free Christmas dinners as incentives to stop them bunking off to play as the game’s dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia.
Narendra Modi, India’s prime minister, took a different approach in a country with an estimated 550 million gamers. Modi posted 10 images on X modelled ‌on the game’s artwork that compared India today with the time of GTA V’s release.
The Indian politician, who has stepped up efforts to appeal to younger voters sinceyouth-led protests over jobs and education, wrote: “India is playing a whole new game!”
View image in fullscreenThe latest instalment of the crime adventure comes 13 years after GTA V was released.Photograph: Rockstar Games
Downing Street said Andy Burnham would not be playing the new instalment. Asked whether the UK prime minister would be exploring Vice City, the Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar’s fictional take on Miami, a spokesperson said: “His diary is very full.”
The launch of GTA VI generated more than 2.6m posts on social media in 24 hours, according to social media monitor Visibrain.
Approximately 1,850 messages about the game were published per minute – 7% more than the number of posts at the start of the 2026 men’s Fifa World Cup.
Among the game’s fans is Sean Little, a self-employed painter and decorator. He persuaded his wife and daughter to sign a“non-interference contract”, giving him a week off dad duties to play in peace in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland.
Myles_Away, a UK-based streamer on the Twitch platform, told the BBC he planned to play for “13 or 14 hours” on Thursday.
He said: “I played all last night, and then I slept, woke up, and [came] right into this interview,” adding: “Obviously not everybody is able to drop the money required. [Consoles] are very expensive at the moment, so they are able to experience the story through streamers.”
Jacob Joel, a 30-year-old IT professional in Bengaluru, southern India, took the day off to play in a gaming cafe. “We waited around 13 long years to get into GTA VI,” he said. “That is a nostalgic feeling.”
In Bangkok, British tourists Kyle McKee and Emily Todd reserved a PS5 console, TV and a sofa at a gaming centre. McKee, 27, told the AFP news agency: “It’s the fear of missing out, honestly.”
The launch also surpassed broadband records in the UK. Virgin Media O2 said its evening traffic between 8pm and 10pm on Wednesday was 9.4% higher than the previous record, set last week by “pre-loading” for GTA VI.
BT and EE networks also recorded their highest-ever home broadband traffic peak in the lead-up to the release.
Data from the two brands found that Fort Augustus, in Loch Ness, Scotland, recorded the biggest percentage uplift in gaming download traffic anywhere in the UK since the start of the pre-downloads last week.
Sony’s shares were up 2.92% on the Tokyo stock exchange after the global launch, with the analytics firm Omdia estimating that GTA VI could generate $3.2bn (£2.4bn) in sales by the end of the year.

Why children lie and it is important they do - BBC News
Image source,Elena HoickaImage caption,
Prof Hoicka's daughter Ada tries to sneakily eat cookie dough aged two when she thought her mum wasn't looking
When drawings appear on the wall or biscuits disappear from the tin, your child might blame the dog or claim there was a ghost - even if they are clutching crayons or covered in crumbs.
Children telling fibs is something most parents experience, but such dishonesty and deception is an important part of mental development.
"It's actually a skill that they're developing and that they will play with in order to get better," clinical psychologist Dr Jade Redfern tells theCBeebies Parenting Downloadpodcast.
Here, experts explain why learning to lie is a sign of healthy behaviour - and how to help encourage honesty.
Prof Hoicka's daughter Juno also deceives her aged three by hiding under a table to eat marshmallows
Young children aren't quite sophisticated enough to lie, says Redfern, but they are capable of deception before the age of one.
One of the studies mentioned on the podcast comes from theUniversity of Bristol,external, which found that around a quarter of children appear to understand some form of deception by the time they are 10 months old.
Prof Elena Hoicka, who led the study, says it was fascinating to see how "surprisingly young" kids could be so adept and cunning, including her own.
"As a mother of three, I can certainly vouch for how artful and wily they can be.
"Hiding under the table or in the bathroom to eat sweets or chocolate is their common ploy."
Hoicka says that the kind of deception a child uses from the age of two is quite basic - like pretending not to hear their parent or denying they've done something.
Clinical psychologist Dr Jade Redfern explains why young children may lie and Traitors winner Rachel Duffy discusses how she encourages hers to tell the truth
"It could also extend to doing forbidden activities in secret," she says. "For example, looking in a bag they were told not to look in when no one is apparently watching, or making excuses, such as claiming to need the toilet when asked to tidy up."
By the age of three, they have become much more proficient and creative in their deceptions, showing a deeper understanding of language and how other people's minds work.
She says they also start to withhold information. For instance, truthfully telling their parents that their sibling has hit them but omitting the fact that they hit their sibling first.
These deceptions are a sign of them developing something Redfern calls "theory of mind".
Ada, age two, deceives her mum by hiding in the bathroom to eat chocolate she had stolen
"As children grow up, we want them to learn and develop the skill that they are their own human being with a separate mind and intentions," she explains.
"This is how [they] develop the skills in empathy, or being able to think about another person's thoughts and feelings that might differ from their own."
Another reason a child might lie is self-preservation as they don't want to upset or disappoint their parent.
"All human beings are driven by attachment," says Redfern. "[Children are] driven by being able to preserve that relationship with their caregivers as they depend upon it."
Early on, they learn what brings them closer to their caregiver and what pulls them apart, she says. With this in mind, Redfern thinks you can encourage honesty by creating a safe environment for a child to tell the truth.
"[We] have to think about ways we can help children feel safe enough to tell us the truth [when] they've made a mistake... and they don't want to disappoint us."
This is something Rachel Duffy, who won the latest series of The Traitors, tells theCBeebies Parentingpodcast that she has been trying to do.
Prof Hoicka with her daughters Ada, now aged six, and Juno who is three years old
The mum-of-threerecalls one occasion when her eldest son borrowed his brother's bike and broke it after crashing it into a car. Initially, he tried to lie about what happened.
"I said to him, 'You'll not get into big trouble when you tell me the truth.' I just left and gave him a little space.
"And he went, 'Yeah, that was me.' And then he knew that space was safe. We had a conversation - no raised voices, no roaring or shouting."
Redfern says this is a good example of how to deal with such a situation and that there are occasions when a lie, or nuance, might be appropriate - such as when they receive a gift they don't want or describe other people physically.
"My kids delightfully told me recently that I was very wrinkly," she says. "Again, I try to take it with open curiosity."
She does this by talking about why they think she is wrinkly.
"I think just being able to explore as children get older, just having open, curious conversations - it really develops empathy for somebody else's feelings when they've been shown and modelled empathy over and over again."

fact_units.text: 4 Random Apps You Might Not Realize Work With Android Auto
Some of these apps will be familiar, while others you may not have heard of.
22, 2026 11:15 am ESTGabriela Vatu for EngadgetAdd Engadget on Google:Preferred SourceGoogle Discover
Android Auto users typically utilize just a few basic apps like Google Maps for directions and Spotify for music.

They don'tdive into the developer menu; they don't make any serious changes to the way Android Auto works; and they don't know they could be spending all those minutes waiting for someone in a parking lotplaying games directly on the car's infotainment display.
But the platform's compatible app library runs much deeper, well beyond navigation and streaming.
Android Auto actually supports a surprising range of communication and meeting tools, like WhatsApp and Google Meet, and even a bunch of other apps to help you navigate more efficiently.
Each one adds layer after layer of functionality that most users never think to explore.
Discovering new apps can genuinely change how you commute while also making it possible to enjoy your drive just a tiny bit more.
Take your work on the road with Google Meet
Android Auto comes with some extra functionality for those in the corporate world, as several popular apps come with Android Auto support for meetings and calls, with Google Meet leading the way.
Because Meet is Google's own app, it fits naturally into the Android Auto experience.
You can see your upcoming meetings on the car display and join a call with a single tap, all in audio-only mode so your eyes stay on the road.
Whether it's a short check-in with your manager or a longer team call, Meet makes it easy to keep up with your schedule even if you have to drive around.
Zoom, Webex by Cisco and Microsoft Teams all work on Android Auto, offering users the opportunity to join video conferences with audio only.
Microsoft Teams, for instance, lets users check their calendar and place calls directly from the car display.
Google Meet also displays upcoming meetings on your schedule.
These features are particularly useful if you're often traveling from location to location but still have to participate in meetings along the way.
They also help if you have to leave early to pick up the kids from school while a meeting is still on your calendar.
One thing to mention about these apps is that, depending on your employer, restrictions may apply.
Certain companies require corporate apps like Google Meet and Microsoft Teams to run inside an isolated Android Work Profile.
In such situations, Android Auto may block calendar sync or prevent the app from appearing on the screen.
There's aWork Mode in the works on Android Auto, though, so it may soon be easier to reach all those apps that are locked out by your employer.
With gas prices being what they are these days, it's more important than ever to know where to fuel up.
Apps likeFueliocan help with that when you're looking for a place to put gas in your car without breaking the bank.
Fuelio tracks fill-ups, odometer readings and fuel prices, then calculates your average fuel economy and cost per mile over time.
You can even use various filters to display gas stations that were updated within the past day, or those that are most appreciated by users.
Google Maps and other similar tools can surface the nearest gas stations and even tell you the latest prices, but Fuelio gives more in-depth information regarding fuel type, distance and more.
Plus, when you throw in all the other features, it's a much better fit if you want to know exactly how much your car is costing you.
While Fuelio is free to use with Android Auto, there is a premium version available that costs money.
If you're driving an EV, then the app you absolutely must use through Android Auto isPlugShare.
This free tool (the paid version removes ads) gives you access to a crowd-sourced map that lets you see the nearest charging stations along your route.
Its real strength is the community behind it, because drivers leave real-time feedback, uploading photos of the charger layout, reporting broken plugs and checking in after charging.
That gives you a clear picture of what to expect before you pull in, so a station that looks fine on paper but has been out of service for days won't catch you off guard.
There are loads of filters you can play with, letting you choose the exact plug type, charging speed and network.
You can also check which amenities are nearby, such as restrooms or a place to grab coffee while you wait.
It's also a great tool for long-distance drives, as it automatically recommends charging stops along the way based on your specific EV model's range.
That goes a long way toward easing the range anxiety that comes with getting an electric car.
The one downside is that the data is only as good as its contributors, so stations in less-traveled areas may have fewer recent reports.

George Hirst takes the plaudits from the Stoke fans
after scoring the winner against Birmingham.Photograph: Cody Froggatt/PAView image in fullscreenGeorge Hirst takes the plaudits from the Stoke fans
after scoring the winner against Birmingham.Photograph: Cody Froggatt/PA
Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return
The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit
There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke satsecond in the Championship tableand were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight.
Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.
Championship roundup: Strelec sends Middlesbrough top; 10-man Stoke go secondRead more
Facing a Birmingham side who arrived top of the table and with firmly held Premier League ambitions, Stoke dominated for an hour, the hitherto goal-shy George Hirst earning a well-deserved lead to send a bumper crowd into raptures. The hand-wringing that then followed Luca Bombino’s sending-off with half an hour remaining made the victory that followed all the sweeter. The 10 men of Stoke were superb. It was no surprise that it took considerable time to convince those in the stands to depart for home after the final whistle.
You see, it is not just that Stoke are second in the table, kept off top spot by goal difference. It is not even that they are undoubtedly the Championship’s form side, with just one defeat in their past 13 games. It is the whole feeling around the place; the resilience Robins has developed, and the belief that they can take on the big guns and beat them.
“We are a work in progress, but today was that step in quality against different opponents. A step up in class,” said Robins. “I thought we were really, really good. The intensity, bravery and the intent that we showed was everything that we asked for.
“And, on the back of that, you’ve got the support that are absolutely right behind us. They trust the players. That is a really good feeling. It’s a great feeling for the players. It’s a heady mix, really.”
Eight years have passed since Stoke were last in the top flight; eight years spent as the Championship equivalent of a sea sponge, doing the bare minimum to survive and letting defeats wash over them while remaining resolutely attached to the rocks of the bottom half of the table. During that time they have ended every campaign no higher than 14th and no lower than 18th. Now, something altogether different is afoot. And this may well be the win that convinces supporters to trust their upbeat instincts.
View image in fullscreenMark Robins’s Stoke have lost just once in their past 13 Championship matches.Photograph: Cody Froggatt/PA
There was an unavoidable fact heading into Saturday’s game. Stoke’s four defeats this season had all come when tasked with opponents fighting at the top end of the table in Swansea, Southampton, Wolves and Middlesbrough. They had shown themselves capable against much of the division, but a failure to deliver against another Championship heavyweight would have raised legitimate questions about their realistic aspirations.
The three August defeats at the start of the campaign preceded the departure of their best player, Sorba Thomas. His replacement, Jack McGlynn, has been an inspired signing. That this victory came without the talismanic figure of Ethan Galbraith, who was absent through illness, is considerable.
As well as switching to a three-man defence following those season-opening losses, a key factor in their upturn has been the restoration of a touch of old-school Stoke; a physicality that was frequently evident on a cold Saturday afternoon.
Bobby Madley, the referee, did not always take kindly to such an approach – to the indignation of the home crowd, who frequently made their feelings clear – but there was no complaint over Bombino’s sending-off for a second yellow after a rash challenge that left him head in hands before the card had even been shown. Tears followed on his slow trudge towards the tunnel, but he need not have worried, with Birmingham barely threatening thereafter.
Given just five points separate the top eight in the Championship table, it would come as no great shock to see Stoke drop off at some point. They do not have the financial benefit of recent Premier League parachute payments or big-spending owners, they are not prolific goalscorers, and a look at their expected goals and expected points tallies shows them firmly in the bottom half of the table. But they are finding ways to win and if McGlynn has a habit of scoring from unexpectedly long distances, perhaps it is because he is good at it.
Before this weekend, Robins had revealed that a top-eight finish was the pre-season target. “You aim for the stars and hopefully you land trying to grab hold of one,” he had said, rather poetically.
If promotion is a “P” they dare not yet speak of, another one – playoffs – is becoming an increasingly realistic proposition. No more sticking to a rock. Swim free and prosper.

Following leaked drone footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session, the Manchester United boss questioned why someone would want to film and share the clips online
Mauricio Pochettino has questioned what could have been gained from the drone footage of a Manchester United training session ahead of his first game in charge against Liverpool.
A 12-minute videotaken over United's Carrington training ground showed the Argentine overseeing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepared for a trip to Anfield on Sunday, live onSky Sports.
The operator has since apologisedand taken down the video, but footage has been viewed over eight million times on reposts from other X accounts and has since been reuploaded by several other YouTube channels, collectively attracting hundreds of thousands of views.
Sky Sports News understandsthe club do not plan on taking legal action, but will not rule out doing so in the future if further incidents occur, and Pochettino questioned the motivation behind the filming.
Watch the best bits of Mauricio Pochettino's first press conference as Manchester United head coach
"What are you going to find?" Pochettino said in an exclusive interview withSky Sports. "We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.
"What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?
"I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about. For sure, something will happen."
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola admitted that he was sent the footage after it was released, but said that the act should've been illegal.
Sky Sports' football correspondent Dan Khan explains the extraordinary story that Pochettino's first Manchester United training session has been leaked after a drone flew over Carrington
"They sent me it yesterday, the footage. But the important part of this is it shouldn't be legal," Iraola said in his pre-match press conference.
"Yesterday you had access to our training, the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes of our training. You know who trained with us, you know who didn't train but it's not a matter of the advantage. It's the fact someone can do this.
"There is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club."

'Head coach? Manager? The title doesn't matter'
Away from the training footage, Pochettino was quizzed on how much influence he wants to have over the club as he looks to become the man to finally restore glory at Old Trafford.
The Argentine has officially been appointed as head coach, the same as predecessors Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick. That was a point of contention from the former during the final press conference before his sacking, as he defiantly labelled himself the manager.
Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim was keen to reiterate he came to the club to be a manager not a coach in his final press conference
However, the term doesn't bother Pochettino as he still hopes to be involved in all the key decisions as time progresses.
"I know that I'm the head coach. I am the guy who is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I'm going to pick the starting XI," he said.
"I'm going to make the changes, and of course, in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen in the squad.
"Sometimes I worked much better when I was head coach or when I was coach than manager.
"It's not necessarily the case that if you are manager, you make all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and you have more power in the decisions. It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, the relationship, with all the areas there."
Captain Bruno remains very important to Poch
Another point of contention at United remains the future of club captain Bruno Fernandes.

Tom Jackson, the formerDenver Broncoslinebacker who spent almost three decades at ESPN, died at the age of 75, the network announced.
Jackson played college football at Louisville, where he spent three seasons playing under Lee Corso before the Broncos took him in the fourth round of the 1973 NFL Draft. Jackson played 13 years in the NFL, all with Denver, making the Pro Bowl three times and eventually earning a spot in the Broncos Ring of Fame.
However, it was Jackson's post-playing career that helped him rise to popularity. Jackson joined ESPN in 1987 immediately after retiring, where he paired up with Chris Berman on "NFL Primetime" and "Sunday NFL Countdown" until 2016. Jackson and Berman became a beloved duo covering football on ESPN, as "NFL Primetime" became a hit studio show because of those two.
Berman announced Jackson's death on "Sunday NFL Countdown" this morning, calling him "one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet."

Tom Jackson, a foundational player on theDenver Broncos' "Orange Crush" defense and a fixture at ESPN as a Hall of Fame broadcaster, died Friday. He was 75.
Jackson's family informed ESPN of his death. A fourth-round pick by the Broncos in the 1973 draft out of Louisville, Jackson played in 191 regular-season games, including 177 starts. He also played in 10 playoff games over 14 seasons with the Broncos.
However, more football fans knew Jackson through his second career act. He had a 29-year run at ESPN and was a mainstay alongside Chris Berman.
Berman said Sunday that Jackson's death was "unexpected" and said he spoke with his longtime partner "at length" on Tuesday.
"He was a vital 75," Berman said on ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown."
"Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock."
The entire studio crew on "Sunday NFL Countdown" wore orange ties during Sunday's show to honor Jackson.
In a statement released by ESPN, Berman said that Jackson was "one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet."
"All of us are stunned," Berman said in his statement. "I'm stunned, we're stunned and you're stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week."
ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said Jackson was "one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN's history."
"He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans," Pitaro said in a statement. "Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends. In fact, ESPN's NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio, a distinction unmatched in our history and a fitting tribute to their lasting impact.
"Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure."
Before the internet and NBC took over the Sunday night package in 2006, "NFL Primetime" was must-see viewing for fans and players because it showed highlights from all the games, as well as the interplay between Berman and Jackson, who often finished each other's sentences.
ESPN's NFL studio in Bristol, Connecticut, is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio. It is the only named studio on ESPN's campus.
When Jackson retired from the network in 2016 -- his final assignment was the Pro Football Hall of Fame's enshrinement ceremony that year -- Berman said: "Tom long ago became almost a brother to me. I know every day he appeared on ESPN was a treasure for football fans."
Jackson often said that he had been "blessed to work for two companies in my life: the Denver Broncos and ESPN." He returned for a digital-only edition of "NFL Primetime" in 2019, reuniting with Berman.

Roy Coyle: Legendary Irish League manager dies aged 80 - BBC Sport
Image source,Press EyeImage caption,
Coyle won 13 Irish League titles during an astonishing coaching career
ByLauren McCannBBC Sport NI Journalist
Roy Coyle, the most successful manager in Irish League history, has died at the age of 80.
Coyle won 13 league titles during his 32-year managerial career, achieving periods of sustained success with Linfield and Glentoran.
He also managed Ards, Derry City and Newry City and had a spell as Glentoran director of football.
In a statement, Glentoran said the club were "deeply saddened to announce the passing of Roy Coyle, our former player and manager and one of the greatest figures in our history".
"A league champion in Glentoran colours, Roy went on to become the most successful manager in the club's history. His association with the Oval spanned more than half a century," their statement continued.
"His teams gave supporters some of their most treasured days, while his influence on players and colleagues endured long after his years in the dugout.
"To generations of the Glentoran family, he remained simply 'The Gaffer'."
A minute's applause was held in Coyle's memory before Glentoran's Irish Premiership game against Cliftonville on Friday at Solitude.
Watch: Roy Coyle reflects on legendary Irish League career
Belfast native Coyle moved into management at the age of 29 when he was appointed player-manager of Linfield in November 1975.
A midfielder during his playing days, Coyle had spells with the Glens, Sheffield Wednesday, Grimsby Town and Linfield after starting out with Ballymena United, and he also won five caps for Northern Ireland.
During his 15 years as Blues boss, Coyle won 31 trophies, guiding the club to 10 league titles in just 12 seasons, alongside two Irish Cup successes and an All-Ireland crown in 1981.
"Everyone at Linfield Football Club is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player and manager, Roy Coyle," the club said.
"His remarkable achievements and contribution to one of the most successful periods in Linfield's history will forever be recognised and remembered.
"The thoughts and deepest condolences of everyone at Linfield Football Club are with Roy's family, friends and all who knew him at this sad time."
After his contract was terminated by Linfield in 1990, Coyle had a spell in the League of Ireland with Derry City between two stints at Ards.
In 1997, he took over at Glentoran and transformed their fortunes, leading the east Belfast club to three league titles and four Irish Cups.
Coyle went on to become the most successful in Glentoran's history, winning 17 trophies before his nine-year tenure at the Oval came to an end in 2006.
He had a brief period in charge of Newry City and also returned for three spells as caretaker boss of Glentoran before retiring in 2017.
'One of the greatest figures in Glentoran's history'
Coyle retired from management in 2017 after his third spell as Glentoran interim manager
Glentoran chairman Colin Jess paid tribute to Coyle, who was inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2025.
"Roy was one of the greatest figures in Glentoran's history, and his passing is a profound loss for our club," said Jess.
"He gave generations of supporters some of the happiest days of their lives. People will always remember where they were and who they were with when his teams won those championships and cups. That is a wonderful thing to have given so many people.
"He set high standards and earned lasting respect. His former players continued to call him The Gaffer long after their playing days had ended, and that says so much about his influence and the place he held in their lives."
Jess added: "We will miss seeing Roy at the ground, enjoying his company and talking football with him. It is difficult to imagine the Oval without him.
"Our deepest sympathy goes to Abbie, the whole family and all those closest to Roy. We are immensely grateful for everything he gave Glentoran, and we will remember him with great affection and pride."
Glentoran owner Ali Pour described Coyle's contribution to Glentoran as "extraordinary".
"He helped make the club champions as a player, led it through years of success as manager and continued to serve it long afterwards," added Pour.
"I often asked Roy for his advice on matters at the club. He knew Glentoran so well, and I valued his judgement and hearing how he saw things. I'll miss those conversations.
"The pride with which supporters remember his teams, and the affection his former players have for him, show how deeply his work mattered to people.
"We owe Roy a great debt of gratitude. His achievements are an enduring part of Glentoran, and we will ensure that future generations understand what he gave this club and why he meant so much to it.
"My family and I extend our heartfelt condolences to Roy's family, friends and everyone mourning his loss. He will always have an honoured place at the Oval."
Northern Ireland Football League (NIFL) chief executive Gerard Lawlor said Coyle's contribution to football in Northern Ireland "went far beyond the trophies he won".
"He was a man who dedicated so much of his life to our local game, earning enormous respect across the football community, regardless of club loyalties," their statement continued.
"Roy represented the passion, commitment and pride that make Irish League football so special. His passing marks the loss of one of the great characters and personalities of our game, and his legacy will live on for generations."

Tom Jackson dies at 75: Football world mourns loss of legendary ESPN analyst
Tom Jackson, the formerDenver Broncoslinebacker who spent almost three decades at ESPN, died at the age of 75, the network announced.
Jackson played college football at Louisville, where he spent three seasons playing under Lee Corso before the Broncos took him in the fourth round of the 1973 NFL Draft.
Jackson played 13 years in the NFL, all with Denver, making the Pro Bowl three times and eventually earning a spot in the Broncos Ring of Fame.
However, it was Jackson's post-playing career that helped him rise to popularity.
Jackson joined ESPN in 1987 immediately after retiring, where he paired up with Chris Berman on "NFL Primetime" and "Sunday NFL Countdown" until 2016.
Jackson and Berman became a beloved duo covering football on ESPN, as "NFL Primetime" became a hit studio show because of those two.
Berman announced Jackson's death on "Sunday NFL Countdown" this morning, calling him "one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet."
“We’ve lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet.” Chris Berman announces the death of his longtime broadcast partner and best friend, Tom Jackson.
Thank you, TJ ❤️ https://t.co/0eogqMa73r
— NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL)November 22, 2026
Jackson's standing in the football world is apparent, as so many people spoke out to mourn his loss.
Before Jackson was an analyst, he was a linebacker for both Louisville and the Broncos, and he left both of those teams as one of the best in their history.
The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history.
— Denver Broncos (@Broncos)November 22, 2026
TJ carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country.
A statement from the Broncos on the passing of legendary Ring of Fame linebacker and Hall of Fame broadcaster Tom Jackson.
We are deeply saddened by the passing of Hall of Fame broadcaster, former Denver Bronco and Cardinal Forever, Tom Jackson.
Our thoughts are with his family, friends, teammates and everyone who knew him.
— Louisville Football (@LouisvilleFB)November 22, 2026
However, so many sports fans know Jackson as a great NFL analyst on "NFL Primetime," and that's exactly how they will remember Jackson.
NFL commissioner Roger Goodell: “The NFL lost a wonderful man with the passing of Tom Jackson.
Along with millions of fans, I will always remember him as a player and broadcaster, but also as a friend.
He was an outstanding player whose toughness and leadership helped define an era of Broncos football.
He brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did, and generations of fans came to know him through his work at ESPN.
Tom helped fans enjoy and better understand football, always bringing the perspective of someone who loved the game and the people who play it.
More importantly, he earned the respect and friendship of players, coaches and everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him.”
— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter)November 22, 2026
@richeisen pays tribute to Tom Jackson, a man who was such a huge part of NFL Sundays for so many of us ❤️ https://t.co/i3MNXBh4zr
— NFL Network (@nflnetwork)November 22, 2026
"Tom was a Hall of Famer in every sense of the word." Our friend Tom Jackson left a lasting impact on everyone around him ❤️ https://t.co/GuwqkneMIJ
— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter)November 22, 2026
I pray that Mort is greeting our great friend Tom Jackson at the heavenly gates this morning.
My condolences to TJ’s wife and daughters as they grieve this loss.
I had the enormous pleasure of covering his career with the Broncos as I began my own as a journalist.
I wrote one of my favorite ledes in a story about his retirement from the NFL.
We became colleagues at ESPN and friends as we spent a golf weekend together supporting the @tcjayfund.

Before John Elway, the Broncos were led by their Orange Crush defense and one of their leaders was an undersized linebacker from Louisville, a man with passion and charisma and unique playmaking ability.
I thank God for TJ and ask that his soul be eternally blessed and strength provided to his grieving family.

COP31 climate deal in doubt after European Union rejects draft | Euronews
ByNathan RennoldsPublished on22 November 2026 - 8:50 GMT+1,Updated12:58ShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsappCopy/paste the article video embed link below:Copied
The latest draft again failed to mention fossil fuels, which have become a flashpoint at the talks.
The European Union has formally rejected the latest COP31 draft deal, saying it cannot accept an agreement that does not mention fossil fuels.
Darragh O'Brien, the climate and energy minister for Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency, said the EU and its member states "object" to the draft because it "does not meet the moment."
"We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change," O'Brien said.
Panama also rejected the proposed deal.
The announcement could see the chaotic and late-running climate talks collapse.
A new COP31 draft agreement had been published early on Sunday as nations continued to struggle to reach an accord.
The new draft kept a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy but again failed to mention fossil fuels, deepening divisions at the UN conference - which is being held in Antalya, Turkey.
The latest text needed consensus approval from almost 200 nations at a closing session on Sunday.
An EU official had told the AFP news agency that the draft was a "backwards" step and warned that there was a "very real possibility" of the talks ending without a deal.
"I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday," they said.
"The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight," a German official added.
Planet-heating fossil fuels have become a flashpoint at the talks, which come amid soaring energy prices and simmering global tensions stemming from the Iran war.
A draft deal unveiled earlier this week had called for a sped-up phasing out of fossil fuels. But a second version released on Thursday removed all mentions of the energy sources, forcing negotiators back to the bargaining table.
A group of countries including France and Panama had released a letter on Friday insisting that a deal include "a clear transition away from fossil fuels."
COP31 President Murat Kurum, center, speaks during a plenary session at the COP31 U.N. Climate Summit, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey.Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.
The latest offering acknowledged a previous global deal to transition away from fossil fuels but stopped short of naming them explicitly.
It also kept a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology backed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised by opponents as costly and ineffective at reducing emissions.
"We are very disappointed with how the text looks," Michael Joseph, the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, told AFP.
"I can't honestly say that I'm okay with it passing" as it is, Joseph said, adding that the draft was "quite silent" on fossil fuels.

COP31 ends without deal as EU rejects final text for omitting mention of fossil fuels
EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th-hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, the bloc's presidency said. The issue remains a major point of contention at the summit, which is taking place amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the war in Iran.

UN climate talks collapsed on Sunday as theEuropean Union​and others rejected a final draft deal put forward byCOP31presidentsTurkeyandAustralia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.
The failed talks reflect world governments' struggle this year to muster ambitious action to address the worsening consequences ofclimate change, as wars, economic pressures and other crises compete for their attention.
After more than two weeks of negotiations ​that spilled two days into ‌overtime – making it the longest COP on record – Turkey's conference president Murat Kurum said at the closing plenary that he could see ⁠there was no agreement and confirmed he would not advance any new text.
"There is nothing to do, we did all that we could," he said. "There will be no new text from now on."
He later left the stage in the midst of speeches ‌being delivered by country representatives.
Try againCover image: © France 2403:03
Australia's COP31 President of Negotiations, Chris Bowen, called the outcome "very disappointing" and said disagreements over fuels and climate finance were the ⁠dealbreakers.
The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all was in Copenhagen in 2009.
Darragh O'Brien, minister of climate, energy and the environment of Ireland, onscreen, speaks during a closing plenary session at the COP31 UN climate summit. © Khalil Hamra, AP
Ireland's environment minister Darragh O'Brien said the European Union could not support the proposed deal in part because it made no mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say drive global warming.
"It is unconscionable that ​we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuel, no reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels," he said.
France called the latest proposal a "backward" step.
"Time is ticking and we are not there yet," French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said in a statement.
Belgium's Climate Minister Jean-Luc Crucke said the failure of the deal was a difficult outcome, but appropriate.
"It's ​not the end of multilateralism, but there has to be courage to say no," he said.
Try againCover image: © France 2405:07
Saudi ‌Arabia and other big oil producer countries had lobbied hard to keep their mention out of the text, according to observers at the summit.
Panama also said it could not support the text because it failed to address the scale and urgency of the climate crisis.
This year's COP is the first since the UN's environmental body in Octoberconfirmed the rise in global temperature was set to exceed ‌1.5 degrees Celsius(2.7 degrees Fahrenheit), a threshold countries agreed at Paris climate talks over a decade ago to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify.
Reacting to the news, UN Secretary-GeneralAntonio Guterressaid he was "deeply disappointed" that the talks in ended without consensus.
"I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," Guterres said in a statement.
"Those who profit from the destruction of our planet must never dictate the terms of the fight to save it.Fossil fuelsare driving the climate crisis," he added.
While a blow to efforts to ratchet up international action, the failure to agree a political declaration in Antalya does not erase the obligations agreed by previous UN conferences or remove the technical and legal frameworks governing multilateral action against climate change.
Read moreCOP31 climate talks go into overtime as nations wrangle over fossil fuels omission
GPressure from Saudi Arabia and other oil producers
The failed deal had acknowledged the planet's projected temperature overshoot and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse it.
That was a big ask ​from oil-producing countries.
While scientists say removing carbon from the atmosphere – when paired with steep emissions cuts – is vital to ​avoiding the worst impacts of climate change, critics of the proposed deal said they worried the carbon removal language would be used as a licence to keep pumping oil.
A representative for the Saudi delegation, which supported the deal's mention of carbon removal, told the summit ​at the closing plenary that he was surprised at the resistance to technology, which he said offered a concrete solution.
Developing countries had also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient new climate finance to help them adapt to a warming planet. The deal had called for a tripling of such finance, but did not specify from what baseline.
The failed deal had also included a goal put forward by Turkey to expand electricity's share of total final world energy consumption to 35% by 2035, from around 23% now.
Proponents of that pledge said it could cut greenhouse gas emissions ⁠by speeding the transition away from fuel-powered cars, furnaces, and other equipment. But critics said it could force more costs onto poor nations without providing a clear path away from fossil fuels.
The COP process is the main vehicle ⁠through which countries coordinate their efforts ​to curb global warming. Its annual meeting provides an opportunity for nations to signal they are willing to work together to find solutions and help finance the problems rising temperatures cause.

United Nations climate talks fell into disarray as the European Union and others rejected a final draft deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkiye and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.
After nearly two weeks of negotiations, which were due to end on Friday but stretched into the weekend, Turkiye’s COP31 President Murat Kurum said at Sunday’s closing plenary that a deal was not approved.

“It is clear that there are parties in this hall who oppose this text. We recognise that there is no consensus on this document. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted,” he said.
The last time UN climate talks failed to end with a deal adopted by all was in Copenhagen in 2009.
The final draft of the deal was released earlier on Sunday, two days after the conference in Antalya was scheduled to end, as the UN climate talks pushed into record extra time.
If it had been approved, it would have acknowledged for the first time that global ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠warming is on course to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) threshold that countries had sought to preserve, while calling for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse the overshoot.
The draft omitted mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say are driving climate change, an issue that has been at the centre of frictions at the talks. Instead, it included language referring to ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌a previous COP at which governments had agreed to transition away from oil, gas and coal.
The EU expressed its disappointment and rejection of the draft deal.
Ireland’s Climate and Energy Minister Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said the bloc and its member states “object” to the pact because it “does not meet the moment”.
“We will not endorse a cover decision, or an Antalya Pact, that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” O’Brien told a chaotic closing session a record 44 hours after the summit’s official end.
Panama, a vocal critic of the COP process that had threatened to walk away from the talks, also formally objected to the proposed deal as the summit plunged into a tumultuous finale.
The proposed deal needed consensus approval from nearly 200 nations, but many states had expressed frustration as the draft did not make reference to coal, oil or gas.
“We will not accept negotiating backwards in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” said O’Brien.
Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks, which come against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.
French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said the proposal was a “backward” step.
“Time is ticking, and we are not there yet,” she said.
An earlier draft had also provoked strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels, the largest contributors to climate change.
Environmental group 350.org said it was disappointed by the continued omission in the new draft, as well as its encouragement of carbon-removal technologies.
“Carbon capture is one of the biggest scams of the overshoot era and our leaders are on ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠the verge of falling for it,” said Sara Shaw, the group’s campaigns and networks ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠director, referring to the practice of trapping carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere.
Kurum said he ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠believed concerns around fossil fuels had ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌been addressed, as had those ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌around helping developing countries finance their adaptation to climate change.
The new ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌leading the talks; Turkiye, which is hosting the meeting; and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.
Climate-related disasters around the globe
The summit’s agreement was meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which drives heatwaves, floods and other disasters.
The gathering had been under pressure to show progress on tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia.
Anopening draftfrom Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers reportedly objected.
Key issues that slowed the agreement included how much effort countries should make to wean themselves off fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and gas.
Other issues included whether to encourage industrial carbon capture and storage of pollutants, as well as whether ramping up electricity generation should only be done with renewables, such as wind and solar, or also involve other sources such as natural gas and coal.
To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut fossil fuel emissions.
In the lead-up to these talks, the UN said the world would likely blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial temperatures.

Cop31 president Murat Kurum chairs a plenary session during Cop31.Photograph: Yasin Akgül/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCop31 president Murat Kurum chairs a plenary session during Cop31.Photograph: Yasin Akgül/AFP/Getty Images
Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected
EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels
Cop31 live blog: longest climate summit ever faces collapse
The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks inTurkey.
The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required. [It] does not even mention fossil fuels.”
As the talks, scheduled to end on Friday,dragged on into Sundayafternoon in the longest climate summit ever, it was clear that the “Antalya pact”, drafted by the Turkish and Australian joint presidencies of the summit, would not achieve the consensus needed to pass.
The Antalya pact invites countries to electrify their economies, calls for rich countries to provide finance to the poor to help them adapt to the impacts of the climate crisis, and calls on countries to minimise the “overshoot” of the 1.5C global heating threshold, of the Paris agreement.
But it failed to endorse the “transition away from fossil fuels” that more than 130 countries demanded, and included controversial provisions on “carbon capture and storage” (CCS) technology that some have said perpetuates fossil fuels.
1:35EU officials reject Cop31 deal as it 'doesn't speak to reality of the climate crisis' – video
The presidencies avoided outright collapse of the “conference of the parties” by passing decisions on various related matters, including the “just transition” to help workers in high-carbon industries shift to a low-carbon economy.
But Murat Kurum, Turkey’s Cop president, acknowledged there was no agreement on the draft “cover decision” text and so it had not been adopted.
“We have done our utmost; ultimately, we have not imposed this text on anyone, nor have we issued an ultimatum ⁠such as a ‘take it or leave it’ demand,” he said. “It is clear that there are parties in this hall who oppose this text. We recognise ⁠that there is no consensus on this document. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted.”
Many countries, including the EU, UK and developing countries including small island states and some of the poorest countries, said they could not support the Antalya pact deal, which was supposed to be main outcome of the Cop.
In a dramatic intervention, O’Brien said on behalf of the EU that it could not accept the final text in its current form. “It fails to meet the moment … We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.” He said the EU would not accept a decision “that greenwashes fossil fuels”.
His intervention was met by applause from the hall, and was later followed by similar objections from Panama, the Marshall Islands and Norway.
“This feels like a real line in the sand moment. Countries are standing up to fossil fuel interests and saying no,” said Bill Hare, the chief executive of the advisory group Climate Analytics.
But Mohamed Adow, the director of the thinktank Power Shift Africa, who called it “the worst Cop ever”, said: “The EU has rejected this text, but it cannot wash its hands of the wreckage it helped create ... For countries facing failed harvests, destroyed homes and mounting debt, this amounts to abandonment by the wealthy nations most responsible for the crisis.
“Europe’s hypocrisy is staggering. Its governments demand fossil fuel roadmaps from others while expanding fossil fuels themselves.”
Saudi Arabia defended the decision to include CCS in the text. Other countries, including the Africa group, China and Pakistan, also did not object to the deal, despite some having reservations. Pakistan told the conference that just because a few items in the pact were objectionable to some, the rest should not be sacrificed: “Climate action is not a menu from which we can select only what suits us.”
Ghana also had criticisms of the process but did not reject the final text: “Africa has always chosen to build multilateralism rather than walk away from it.”
View image in fullscreenDarragh O’Brien (centre) and Wopke Hoekstra, the EU climate commissioner, speak outside a plenary session at Cop31 on Sunday.Photograph: Khalil Hamra/AP
Close to 200 countries have been meeting in Antalya for a fortnight under the joint presidencies of Turkey and Australia, with the overrunning talks marked by long periods of deadlock as countries failed to find common ground.
The Cop co-president, Australia’s climate change minister, Chris Bowen, defended his leadership. “Australia left nothing on the field,” he said, but the red lines the presidencies had tried to negotiate were “unbridgeable”.
Asked about the consensus-based system that broke down at the talks, Simon Stiell, the executive secretary of the UN framework convention on climate change, said: “It certainly fell short today,” while emphasising that a significant number of agenda items were passed, with “real progress and concrete results”.
But for many participants, these talks exposed a failure of collective will, particularly of the rich world, to confront the urgency of the climate crisis.
While extreme weather around the world has worsened this year, claiming tens of thousands of lives in heatwaves, in disasters such as the glacier collapse in Nepal, and in droughts and floods worsened by the superchargedEl Niño, the slow speed of the climate negotiations appalled even veteran participants.
“There isn’t the sense of urgency to address these issues. That to me is very frustrating,” said Mary Robinson, a former president of Ireland and former UN climate envoy, as the talks neared their scheduled close. “We have co-presidents who haven’t really been stepping up and giving that leadership.”

Nhà rường cổ có cấu trúc độc lạ, một nửa căn từng được trả giá 25 tỷ đồng
(Dân trí) - Tại phố cổ Bao Vinh (thành phố Huế) hiện còn nhiều công trình gắn với thời kỳ vàng son của khu thương cảng sầm uất một thời. Nổi bật nhất là ngôi nhà rường 2 tầng, có cấu trúc 5 gian rưỡi độc lạ.
Phố cổ Bao Vinh nằm ở vùng hạ lưu sông Hương, thuộc phường Hóa Châu, thành phố Huế.
Phố Bao Vinh hình thành từ đầu thế kỷ XVII và phát triển mạnh mẽ trong giai đoạn thế kỷ XVII-XIX cùng hệ thống cảng thị Thanh Hà - Bao Vinh. Đây là một trong những thương cảng sầm uất của xứ Đàng Trong.
Trải qua nhiều biến đổi, phố Bao Vinh mất dần vai trò thương cảng, nhưng người dân nơi đây vẫn giữ được một số ngôi nhà cổ như những chứng tích của một thời.
Nhà cổ ở Bao Vinh thuộc kiểu nhà rường truyền thống Huế nhưng kết hợp yếu tố thương mại vốn hình thành từ xa xưa. Tại phố cổ này, ngôi nhà ở số 77A-77B Bao Vinh nổi lên như một công trình mang tính biểu tượng và là điểm nhấn kiến trúc khác biệt nhất.
Ông Phan Gia Đắc (76 tuổi), chủ nhân của 3 gian nhà số 77A, cho biết công trình được làm bằng gỗ gõ và lim quý hiếm từ thời vua Khải Định, cách đây hơn 100 năm. Ngôi nhà cao 2 tầng, cấu trúc 5 gian rưỡi độc lạ.
Trong khi đại đa số nhà rường truyền thống chỉ có một tầng và thường có cấu trúc 3 gian 2 chái, công trình ở số 77A-77B Bao Vinh lại không có chái. Ông Đắc cho rằng, đây là một biến thể cực kỳ hiếm hoi của kiến trúc nhà rường truyền thống Huế.
Theo ông Đắc, ngôi nhà hiện chia làm 2 phần. 3 gian ở số 77A hiệngia đìnhông Đắc ở và thờ tổ tiên. Hơn 2 gian còn lại tại số 77B, gia đình bà Phan Thị Diệu Liên (cô ruột của ông Đắc) đang ở.
Trong nhà ông Phan Gia Đắc còn lưu giữ bức hoành phi (tấm biển) sơn son thếp vàng có từ thời vua Khải Định. Bức hoành phi khắc 3 chữ Hán "di lệnh danh" với ý nghĩa để lại để lại tiếng thơm tốt đẹp cho đời sau. Đã từng có người liên hệ ông Đắc trong suốt 3 năm để hỏi mua lại món đồ này.
Ngoài ra, gia đình ông Phan Gia Đắc còn lưu giữ nhiều món đồ cổ do các đời trước truyền lại như tranh ảnh, tủ chè, đồ gốm thời nhà Minh (Trung Quốc),...
Ông Đắc còn sở hữu 2 chiếc xe đạp mang thương hiệu Mercier của Pháp, được sản xuất từ năm 1912.
Ông Đắc luôn tâm niệm ngôi nhà rường truyền thống và những đồ cổ quý hiếm trong nhà đều do các thế hệ trước để lại, bản thân chỉ là người kế thừa nên ông chưa từng nghĩ đến chuyện sang nhượng, mua bán.
Phần còn lại của công trình ở số 77B đã được nhà nước hỗ trợ 1 tỷ đồng để trùng tu vào năm 2024 theo đề án "Chính sách hỗ trợ bảo vệ và phát huy giá trị nhà rường cổ Bao Vinh, phường Hương Vinh cũ (nay là phường Hóa Châu)".
Bà Phan Thị Diệu Liên (85 tuổi, chủ nhà) cho biết đã có người trả gia đình 25 tỷ đồng để mua lại phần nhà gia đình đang sở hữu nhưng bà từ chối.
"Có người còn trả 15 triệu đồng/tháng thuê nhà đểkinh doanhnhưng tôi cũng từ chối. Gia đình sẽ gìn giữ ngôi nhà này, góp phần bảo tồn phố cổ Bao Vinh", bà Liên chia sẻ.
Tại phố cổ Bao Vinh, có nhiều ngôi nhà rường cổ khác cũng được nhà nước hỗ trợ kinh phí để trùng tu, bảo tồn. Bà Nguyễn Thị Thanh Huyền, Phó trưởng Phòng Văn hóa - Xã hội phường Hóa Châu, cho biết tại khu phố cổ Bao Vinh hiện còn 14 ngôi nhà rường cổ và 7 nhà tứ giác có kiến trúc đặc thù.
UBND thành phố Huế đã lựa chọn 7 ngôi nhà rường cổ do gia đình tự nguyện đăng ký tham gia đề án "Chính sách hỗ trợ bảo vệ và phát huy giá trị nhà rường cổ Bao Vinh, giai đoạn 2023-2026" để bảo tồn, trùng tu.
Những ngôi nhà tứ giác nằm dọc bờ sông Hương ở phố cổ Bao Vinh được xây dựng từ hàng trăm năm trước.
Mới đây, UBND phường Hóa Châu đã phê duyệt dự án dự án quảng trường ven sông Hương tại phố cổ Bao Vinh, với tổng mức đầu tư hơn 200 tỷ đồng.
Theo kế hoạch, chính quyền địa phương sẽ di dời, giải tỏa dãy nhà ở khu vực dọc bờ sông, giữ lại các ngôi nhà tứ giác cổ và bến thuyền để làm phố đi bộ.
Vị trí phố cổ Bao Vinh trên bản đồ (Ảnh: Google Maps).
Bà Phan Thị Diệu Liên cho biết nguồn gốc gia đình ở ngoài Bắc, sau đó vào vùng Thuận Hóa lập nghiệp. Ban đầu, các thế hệ trước trong gia đình bà Liên sinh sống tại vùng Sịa (nay thuộc xã Quảng Điền, thành phố Huế), một nơi khá phát triển ở xứ Đàng Trong trước đây.
Khi khu thương cảng Bao Vinh phát triển mạnh, gia đình này đã mua đất, chuyển lên buôn bán tại đây, từng sở hữu tàu thuyền lớn để đi thua mua hàng hóa. Cả ông nội và cha của bà đều là những thương gia lớn ở khu thương cảng Bao Vinh xưa.
Ông Phan Gia Đắc từng nghe ông nội kể ngôi nhà rường làm ròng rã 2 năm mới hoàn thành, trở thành công trình bề thế nhất khu phố. Một vị quan lớn nghe tiếng đã đích thân cưỡi ngựa về chiêm ngưỡng.
Trải qua quá trình tồn tại, có giai đoạn ngôi nhà bị xuống cấp. Trong khoảng thời gian năm 2005-2010, ông Đắc đã bỏ ra nhiều tiền để thuê thợ giỏi về sửa chữa, tôn tạo 3 gian nhà mà ông được kế thừa.
Nhiều ngôi nhà rường mới được lắp dựng tại khu vực Phủ Nội vụ, bên trong di tích Đại nội Huế, khiến nhiều người thắc mắc về tính hợp pháp của các công trình này.
Loạt nhà rường mới trong Đại nội Huế chờ thí điểm mô hình đối tác công tư
Thành phố Huế đang xây dựng đề án và xin chủ trương thí điểm khai thác các dịch vụ liên quan bên trong khu vực di tích Đại nội theo phương thức đối tác công tư (PPP).
Bắt đầu tháo dỡ nhà rường trái phép trong lăng Hoàng thái hậu Từ Dũ
Công trình huỳnh ốc theo kiểu nhà rường truyền thống trong khu vực lăng mộ của Hoàng thái hậu Từ Dũ ở Huế sẽ hoàn thành tháo dỡ trong vài ngày tới.
Từng là kinh đô của Việt Nam từ đầu thế kỷ XIX đến giữa thế kỷ XX, Huế mang nhiều đặc trưng với phủ đệ, nhà rường là nơi sinh sống của các bậc tao nhân mặc khách.
1.Bất ngờ lý do cô dâu tự lái xe hoa chở chú rể hơn 200km trong ngày tân hôn
2.Người mẹ ở Phú Thọ tặng cô giáo gà nhà tự nuôi, kèm gừng sả lá chanh
3.Tài xế cứu thanh niên định nhảy cầu ngại ngùng vì lời cô giáo nói với con
4.Vụ trống đồng mất tung tích 32 năm: Công bố kết quả giám định
