Phố Bao Vinh hình thành từ đầu thế kỷ XVII và phát triển mạnh mẽ trong giai đoạn thế kỷ XVII-XIX cùng hệ thống cảng thị Thanh Hà - Bao Vinh.
Đây là một trong những thương cảng sầm uất của xứ Đàng Trong.
Trải qua nhiều biến đổi, phố Bao Vinh mất dần vai trò thương cảng, nhưng người dân nơi đây vẫn giữ được một số ngôi nhà cổ như những chứng tích của một thời.
Nhà cổ ở Bao Vinh thuộc kiểu nhà rường truyền thống Huế nhưng kết hợp yếu tố thương mại vốn hình thành từ xa xưa.
Tại phố cổ này, ngôi nhà ở số 77A-77B Bao Vinh nổi lên như một công trình mang tính biểu tượng và là điểm nhấn kiến trúc khác biệt nhất.
Ông Phan Gia Đắc (76 tuổi), chủ nhân của 3 gian nhà số 77A, cho biết công trình được làm bằng gỗ gõ và lim quý hiếm từ thời vua Khải Định, cách đây hơn 100 năm.
Ngôi nhà cao 2 tầng, cấu trúc 5 gian rưỡi độc lạ.
Trong khi đại đa số nhà rường truyền thống chỉ có một tầng và thường có cấu trúc 3 gian 2 chái, công trình ở số 77A-77B Bao Vinh lại không có chái.
Ông Đắc cho rằng, đây là một biến thể cực kỳ hiếm hoi của kiến trúc nhà rường truyền thống Huế.
Theo ông Đắc, ngôi nhà hiện chia làm 2 phần.
3 gian ở số 77A hiệngia đìnhông Đắc ở và thờ tổ tiên.
Hơn 2 gian còn lại tại số 77B, gia đình bà Phan Thị Diệu Liên (cô ruột của ông Đắc) đang ở.
Trong nhà ông Phan Gia Đắc còn lưu giữ bức hoành phi (tấm biển) sơn son thếp vàng có từ thời vua Khải Định.
Bức hoành phi khắc 3 chữ Hán "di lệnh danh" với ý nghĩa để lại để lại tiếng thơm tốt đẹp cho đời sau.
Đã từng có người liên hệ ông Đắc trong suốt 3 năm để hỏi mua lại món đồ này.
Ngoài ra, gia đình ông Phan Gia Đắc còn lưu giữ nhiều món đồ cổ do các đời trước truyền lại như tranh ảnh, tủ chè, đồ gốm thời nhà Minh (Trung Quốc),...
Ông Đắc còn sở hữu 2 chiếc xe đạp mang thương hiệu Mercier của Pháp, được sản xuất từ năm 1912.

Ông Đắc luôn tâm niệm ngôi nhà rường truyền thống và những đồ cổ quý hiếm trong nhà đều do các thế hệ trước để lại, bản thân chỉ là người kế thừa nên ông chưa từng nghĩ đến chuyện sang nhượng, mua bán.

Phần còn lại của công trình ở số 77B đã được nhà nước hỗ trợ 1 tỷ đồng để trùng tu vào năm 2024 theo đề án "Chính sách hỗ trợ bảo vệ và phát huy giá trị nhà rường cổ Bao Vinh, phường Hương Vinh cũ (nay là phường Hóa Châu)".
Bà Phan Thị Diệu Liên (85 tuổi, chủ nhà) cho biết đã có người trả gia đình 25 tỷ đồng để mua lại phần nhà gia đình đang sở hữu nhưng bà từ chối.
"Có người còn trả 15 triệu đồng/tháng thuê nhà đểkinh doanhnhưng tôi cũng từ chối.
Gia đình sẽ gìn giữ ngôi nhà này, góp phần bảo tồn phố cổ Bao Vinh", bà Liên chia sẻ.

Ánh Viên có hành động đẹp khi về đích
Màn tái xuất củaNguyễn Thị Ánh Viên(Quân đội) tạo sức hút khi đông đảo người hâm mộ đến CLB Bơi - Lặn Phú Thọ xem cô tranh tài ở chung kết 200 m hỗn hợp nữ diễn ra tối 22.11. Ở vòng loại vào buổi sáng, Ánh Viên về hạng nhì, sau đàn em Võ Thị Mỹ Tiên (Tây Ninh).
Nguyễn Thị Ánh Viên (phải) về hạng nhì ở nội dung 200 m hỗn hợp nữ
Ánh Viên nhận tràng pháo tay thật lớn từ người hâm mộ khi bước ra bể bơi tranh tài chung kết. Có thời điểm, cô vượt lên dẫn đầu trên đường đua nhưng Võ Thị Mỹ Tiên bung sức mạnh mẽ và là người cán đích đầu tiên, đoạt HCV với thành tích 2 phút 14 giây 38 và phá kỷ lục đại hội (kỷ lục cũ 2 phút 19 giây 43 của Ánh Viên). Sau khi về đích, Ánh Viên chủ động choàng tay ôm lấy Mỹ Tiên chia vui với đồng nghiệp.
Kình ngư Việt kiều Mỹ Watson Nguyễn đánh bại Phạm Thanh Bảo ở cự ly 50 m ếch nam
Tại nội dung 50 m ếch,kình ngư Việt kiều MỹWatson Nguyễn (An Giang) khẳng định tài năng khi tiếp tục vượt qua Phạm Thành Bảo (Vĩnh Long), cán đích đầu tiên, đoạt HCV với thành tích 27 giây 07. Thành tích này của Watson Nguyễn phá kỷ lục quốc gia (27 giây 66) lẫn kỷ lục đại hội (28 giây 39).
Kình ngư 17 tuổi Nguyễn Thúy Hiền tỏa sáng với cú đúp HCV
Kình ngư 17 tuổi Nguyễn Thúy Hiền (Quân đội) thi đấu thành công nhất trong ngày đầu tiên của môn bơi khi giành 2 HCV ở nội dung 50 m ếch nữ và 100 m tự do nữ. Ở 50 m ếch nữ, Thúy Hiền đạt thành tích 31 giây 73, phá kỷ lục đại hội (32 giây 46) lẫn kỷ lục quốc gia (31 giây 95). Ở nội dung 100 m tự do, Nguyễn Thúy Hiền đạt thành tích 56 giây 10, phá kỷ lục đại hội (56 giây 99).
Trần Văn Nguyễn Quốc (trái) và Lương Jerremie Loic Nino cán đích cùng lúc và cùng đứng trên bục cao nhất
Đội Đà Nẵng giành HCV tiếp sức 4x200 m tự do nam
Tại nội dung 100 m tự do nam, kình ngư Trần Văn Nguyễn Quốc (Đà Nẵng) và Lương Jerremie Loic Nino (TP.HCM) chạm đích cùng lúc và được công nhận đồng hạng nhất với thành tích 50 giây 03. Trần Hưng Nguyên (Quân đội) đoạt HCV nội dung 400 m hỗn hợp. Đội Đà Nẵng đoạt HCV nội dung tiếp sức 4x200 tự do nam.

Thanh Hóa chỉ đạo hỏa tốc tìm giải pháp cho vùng quê "mưa lớn là ngập lụt" | Báo Dân trí
Sự kiệnMưa lớn ở miền TrungXử lý vi phạm tại 12 dự án của Mường Thanh
Thanh Hóa chỉ đạo hỏa tốc tìm giải pháp cho vùng quê "mưa lớn là ngập lụt"
(Dân trí) - Liên quan đến tình trạng ngập lụt mỗi khi mưa lớn tại xã Nông Cống, lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Thanh Hóa đã chỉ đạo các cơ quan chức năng kiểm tra, đề xuất giải pháp khắc phục.
Ngày 19/11, Văn phòng UBND tỉnh Thanh Hóa cho biết, Phó Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh Cao Văn Cường đã có văn bản hỏa tốc, chỉ đạo kiểm tra tình trạngngập lụtmỗi khi mưa lớn tại xã Nông Cống (Thanh Hóa) sau khi báoDân tríphản ánh.
Theo đó, lãnh đạo tỉnh giao Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường Thanh Hóa chủ trì, phối hợp với Sở Xây dựng Thanh Hóa, UBND xã Nông Cống, Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu và các đơn vị liên quan khẩn trương kiểm tra, xác minh, đề xuất giải pháp xử lý, khắc phục tình trạng ngập lụt.
Các đơn vị phải có văn bản báo cáo UBND tỉnh và trả lời báoDân trítrước ngày 25/11.
Mưa lớn gây ngập lụt tại xã Nông Cống hôm 9/11 (Ảnh: Thanh Tùng).
Trước đó, nhưDân tríđã phản ánh, xã Nông Cống vốn là địa bàn vùng trũng, có sông Yên chảy qua. Những năm trước, mỗi khi mưa lớn, nước từ thượng nguồn đổ về có thể thoát ra các cánh đồng trên địa bàn.
Tuy nhiên, sau khi nhiều tuyến giao thông được xây dựng, một số cánh đồng tại xã Nông Cống bị chia cắt, khiến khả năng tiêu thoát nước không còn thuận lợi như trước.
Điển hình là khu dân cư thôn Vạn Thiện, nơi có tuyến đường nối từ quốc lộ 45 đến nút giao Vạn Thiện thuộc tuyến cao tốc Bắc - Nam đi qua. Người dân địa phương cho biết, kể từ khi tuyến đường này được xây dựng, mỗi khi mưa lớn, việc tiêu thoát nước gặp nhiều khó khăn, dẫn đến tình trạng ngập úng cục bộ.
Tuyến đường cắt ngang cánh đồng khiến việc tiêu thoát lũ gặp khó khăn (Ảnh: Thanh Tùng).
Ông Đồng Minh Quân, Chủ tịch UBND xã Nông Cống, xác nhận tình trạng cứ mưa lớn là ngập lụt đã xuất hiện trên địa bàn trong khoảng 3 năm trở lại đây.
Theo ông Quân, mưa lớn cực đoan, lượng mưa tăng cao là một trong những nguyên nhân khiến tình trạng ngập lụt trên địa bàn diễn ra thường xuyên hơn. Về giải pháp khắc phục, ông Quân cho biết địa phương đang gặp nhiều khó khăn, gần như phải sống chung với lũ.
Hơn 14 tỷ đồng tu sửa cấp thiết khu tháp cổ nghìn tuổi "mưa lớn là ngập"
Tỉnh Cà Mau quyết định dự chi hơn 14 tỷ đồng để đầu tư tu sửa cấp thiết di tích quốc gia đặc biệt khảo cổ Vĩnh Hưng.
Thanh Hóa tiếp tục mưa lớn, có khả năng ngập úng
Ban Chỉ đạo phòng thủ dân sự quốc gia đề nghị Thanh Hóa triển khai lực lượng kiểm tra, chủ động tổ chức di dời, sơ tán người dân khu vực ven sông, suối, trũng thấp, có nguy cơ xảy ra ngập lụt sâu.
Lý do một vùng quê ở Thanh Hóa liên tục ngập lụt mỗi khi mưa lớn
Mưa đã tạnh nhưng hàng trăm ngôi nhà ở xã Nông Cống, Thanh Hóa vẫn ngập trong nước. Người dân và chính quyền địa phương lý giải những nguyên nhân khiến vùng đất này thường xuyên trở thành “rốn lũ”.
Nước dâng cao ngang bụng ở Thanh Hóa, người dân đưa ô tô đi tránh lụt
Gần 900 hộ dân ở xã Nông Cống (Thanh Hóa) bị ngập do mưa lớn kéo dài. Lo nước lụt dâng cao trong đêm, người dân đưa ô tô lên cầu Chuối để tránh ngập.

Ở vòng loại vào buổi sáng, Ánh Viên về hạng nhì, sau đàn em Võ Thị Mỹ Tiên (Tây Ninh).
Nguyễn Thị Ánh Viên (phải) về hạng nhì ở nội dung 200 m hỗn hợp nữ
Ánh Viên nhận tràng pháo tay thật lớn từ người hâm mộ khi bước ra bể bơi tranh tài chung kết.

Có thời điểm, cô vượt lên dẫn đầu trên đường đua nhưng Võ Thị Mỹ Tiên bung sức mạnh mẽ và là người cán đích đầu tiên, đoạt HCV với thành tích 2 phút 14 giây 38 và phá kỷ lục đại hội (kỷ lục cũ 2 phút 19 giây 43 của Ánh Viên).
Sau khi về đích, Ánh Viên chủ động choàng tay ôm lấy Mỹ Tiên chia vui với đồng nghiệp.
Kình ngư Việt kiều Mỹ Watson Nguyễn đánh bại Phạm Thanh Bảo ở cự ly 50 m ếch nam
Tại nội dung 50 m ếch,kình ngư Việt kiều MỹWatson Nguyễn (An Giang) khẳng định tài năng khi tiếp tục vượt qua Phạm Thành Bảo (Vĩnh Long), cán đích đầu tiên, đoạt HCV với thành tích 27 giây 07.
Thành tích này của Watson Nguyễn phá kỷ lục quốc gia (27 giây 66) lẫn kỷ lục đại hội (28 giây 39).
Kình ngư 17 tuổi Nguyễn Thúy Hiền tỏa sáng với cú đúp HCV

Ở 50 m ếch nữ, Thúy Hiền đạt thành tích 31 giây 73, phá kỷ lục đại hội (32 giây 46) lẫn kỷ lục quốc gia (31 giây 95).
Ở nội dung 100 m tự do, Nguyễn Thúy Hiền đạt thành tích 56 giây 10, phá kỷ lục đại hội (56 giây 99).

Trần Hưng Nguyên (Quân đội) đoạt HCV nội dung 400 m hỗn hợp.
Đội Đà Nẵng đoạt HCV nội dung tiếp sức 4x200 tự do nam.

Thanh Hóa chỉ đạo hỏa tốc tìm giải pháp cho vùng quê "mưa lớn là ngập lụt"
(Dân trí) - Liên quan đến tình trạng ngập lụt mỗi khi mưa lớn tại xã Nông Cống, lãnh đạo UBND tỉnh Thanh Hóa đã chỉ đạo các cơ quan chức năng kiểm tra, đề xuất giải pháp khắc phục.

Ngày 19/11, Văn phòng UBND tỉnh Thanh Hóa cho biết, Phó Chủ tịch UBND tỉnh Cao Văn Cường đã có văn bản hỏa tốc, chỉ đạo kiểm tra tình trạngngập lụtmỗi khi mưa lớn tại xã Nông Cống (Thanh Hóa) sau khi báoDân tríphản ánh.

Theo đó, lãnh đạo tỉnh giao Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường Thanh Hóa chủ trì, phối hợp với Sở Xây dựng Thanh Hóa, UBND xã Nông Cống, Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu và các đơn vị liên quan khẩn trương kiểm tra, xác minh, đề xuất giải pháp xử lý, khắc phục tình trạng ngập lụt.
Các đơn vị phải có văn bản báo cáo UBND tỉnh và trả lời báoDân trítrước ngày 25/11.
Mưa lớn gây ngập lụt tại xã Nông Cống hôm 9/11 (Ảnh: Thanh Tùng).
Trước đó, nhưDân tríđã phản ánh, xã Nông Cống vốn là địa bàn vùng trũng, có sông Yên chảy qua.
Những năm trước, mỗi khi mưa lớn, nước từ thượng nguồn đổ về có thể thoát ra các cánh đồng trên địa bàn.
Tuy nhiên, sau khi nhiều tuyến giao thông được xây dựng, một số cánh đồng tại xã Nông Cống bị chia cắt, khiến khả năng tiêu thoát nước không còn thuận lợi như trước.

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr89:
Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say - BBC News
Image source,Planet Labs PBCImage caption,
Satellite imagery showed a ship on fire at the port early on Sunday morning
Published22 November 2026, 15:50 GMT
An explosion has occurred on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port after a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.
The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government.
It added that the site was secured, and there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.
Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC, reviewed by BBC Verify, shows a boat on fire at 0547 GMT at the Benghazi port, with a separate image captured several hours later appearing to show the same vessel partially submerged.
Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship engulfed in flames and smoke, while it is still dark.
The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.
Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.
GNS said the country was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.
Seperately, Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli - the Government of National Unity (GNU) - warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.
GNU said such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".
Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.
Benghazi is more than 2,000 km (1,243 miles) away from the Russian capital Moscow.

According to Ukrainian authorities,nine residents, including one child, had been evacuated. The State Emergency Service initially said that up toseven people could be trapped beneath the rubble. President Volodymyr Zelenskyylater said that14 people were unaccounted for.
The attack was part of a wider wave ofRussian drone strikesreported across Ukraine overnight. Ukraine’s Air Force said186 attack drones were launched, of which 161 were shot down.
InKharkiv, a strike drone hit the Kyivskyi district and started a fire. InChernihiv, a Russian strike set a wood-processing plant ablaze, while inZaporizhzhiathree people, including two children, were injured in an evening attack.
The extent of the destruction inDymerraised fears for residents whomight still be beneath the collapsed sections of the building. article.title: Bruno Fernandes tạm hoãn đàm phán hợp đồng với Manchester United dưới triều đại Pochettino
article.summary: Đội trưởng Manchester United Bruno Fernandes xác nhận đã từ chối các đề nghị gia hạn hợp đồng và tạm dừng toàn bộ đàm phán, khẳng định ưu tiên hàng đầu hiện tại là giúp CLB lấy lại phong độ chiến thắng.
body: Tình hình nhân sự tại Old Trafford tiếp tục thu hút sự chú ý lớn khi đội trưởng Bruno Fernandes chính thức xác nhận anh đã quyết định tạm hoãn các cuộc đàm phán gia hạn hợp đồng với Manchester United. Tiền vệ người Bồ Đào Nha cho biết dù câu lạc bộ đã đưa ra lời đề nghị mới nhằm giữ chân anh, thời điểm hiện tại không phù hợp để tiếp tục thảo luận về các vấn đề tương lai cá nhân.

Theo chia sẻ từ Fernandes, giao kèo hiện tại của anh sẽ đáo hạn vào cuối mùa giải năm nay, mặc dù đội bóng sở hữu điều khoản tự động gia hạn thêm 12 tháng. Tiền vệ 32 tuổi tiết lộ anh từng từ chối hai lời đề nghị gia hạn từ phía câu lạc bộ và bác bỏ những đồn đoán xung quanh yêu cầu tài chính cá nhân. Anh nhấn mạnh động lực của mình không đến từ tiền bạc khi từng có cơ hội chuyển đến những nơi có đãi ngộ cao hơn hoặc điều kiện thời tiết ấm áp hơn trong các kỳ chuyển nhượng trước đó.

Quyết định tạm dừng đàm phán hợp đồng diễn ra trong bối cảnh Manchester United đang trải qua giai đoạn biến động mạnh mẽ về cấu trúc thượng tầng và băng ghế huấn luyện. Mauricio Pochettino vừa chính thức tiếp quản chiếc ghế nóng tại câu lạc bộ, đối mặt với nhiệm vụ vực dậy một tập thể đang ngụp lặn ở nửa dưới bảng xếp hạng Ngoại hạng Anh. Trong bối cảnh đội bóng chuẩn bị bước vào trận đấu gặp Liverpool tại Anfield, Fernandes khẳng định sự tập trung hoàn toàn phải hướng về chuyên môn thay vì các bàn thảo hợp đồng.

Dù phong độ của tuyển thủ Bồ Đào Nha mùa này đã sụt giảm đáng kể so với kỷ lục kiến tạo ở mùa giải trước, anh vẫn được kỳ vọng là nhân tố trọng yếu trong kế hoạch tái thiết của nhà cầm quân người Argentina. Pochettino tiết lộ ông đã có buổi trò chuyện kéo dài ba tiếng đồng hồ với các cầu thủ ngay sau khi tiếp quản đội bóng. Về phần mình, Fernandes khẳng định anh chưa từng có bất kỳ mâu thuẫn nào với cựu huấn luyện viên Michael Carrick và sẵn sàng rời đi ngay lập tức nếu câu lạc bộ cảm thấy anh không còn phù hợp, nhưng hiện tại mục tiêu tối thượng vẫn là đưa đội bóng trở lại mạch chiến thắng.

Amazononly announcedits first digital photo frame less than a month ago, but it’s already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. You can currently grab theAlexa Photo FrameatAmazonandBest Buystarting at $114 ($115 off), making it a great holiday gift for anyone who loves displaying family photos. If you prefer the walnut trim over the birch or standard black models, it’s also on sale atBest Buyfor $134.99 ($95 off) — which, like with the others, is the first discount we’ve seen.
$115$23050% off$115$115 at Amazon (birch)$115 at Best Buy (black)$135 at Best Buy (walnut)
The Alexa Photo Frame features a 10-inch, semi-matte touchscreen that’s designed to make digital photos look more natural, with built-in light sensors that automatically adjust brightness throughout the day. It displays images from Amazon Photos, which supports uploads from both iOS and Android devices, including photos stored in iCloud. You can choose which people or albums to display, or let Alexa Plus do the work, which often results in photos based on your facial expression, the season, and even the lighting. You can also search for specific photos with voice commands, letting you easily pull up images of your first dog, your child as a baby, and other shots without having to scroll endlessly through years of photos yourself.

If you want to add a more personal touch, Amazon also lets you attach voice notes to individual photos via the Amazon Photos app. For example, you can add a recording of your kid explaining their Halloween costume to a trick-or-treating photo. Plus, you can preload the frame with photos and recordings before gifting it, so your loved one won’t have to spend time setting it up.
We’re still testing Amazon’s answer to the Aura frame, but it looks like a particularly good option if you’re already an Amazon Prime member. A Prime subscription grants you unlimited full-resolution photo storage and access to Alexa Plus at no additional cost, and unlike Amazon’s smart displays, the frame doesn’t serve up annoying ads. That said, you don’t need a subscription to use it, and new users can always access a limited-time trial of Alexa Plus.

Thời trang Việt lấy gì cạnh tranh với nhãn ngoại mùa Black Friday?
Giữa cuộc đua khuyến mãi với các nhãn hàng quốc tế dịp Black Friday, local brand Việt (thương hiệu nội địa) tìm cách cạnh tranh bằng giá bán, mẫu mã và khả năng nắm bắt thị hiếu người tiêu dùng.
Các bảng giảm giá từ 30-50% được trưng bày tại cửa hàng, thu hút khách mua sắm - Ảnh: HÀ PHƯƠNG
Những ngày cuối tháng 11, thị trường thời trang TP.HCM bắt đầu sôi động khi nhiều thương hiệu triển khai chương trình ưu đãi đón Black Friday.
Bên cạnh các nhãn hàng quốc tế, nhiều thương hiệu nội địa (local brand) cũng nhập cuộc với mức giảm sâu, hướng đến nhóm khách hàng trẻ. Theo ghi nhận, nhiều thương hiệu thời trang Việt đồng loạt tung chương trình giảm giá đến 70%, có sản phẩm chỉ từ 79.000 đồng.
Giảm giá đến 70%, hàng thời trang từ 79.000 đồng
Ghi nhận củaTuổi Trẻtại một số điểm mua sắm thời trang ở TP.HCM như khu The New Playground, chung cư 26 Lý Tự Trọng, các tuyến đường Nguyễn Trãi, Trần Quang Diệu..., nhiều cửa hàng đồng loạt treo biển giảm giá từ 30-70%, thu hút khách đến lựa chọn, thử đồ.
Không khí mua sắm tại khu The New Playground (TP.HCM) nhộn nhịp trước thềm Black Friday - Ảnh: Hà Phương
Đây là những khu vực được biết đến với các nhãn hàng thời trang trong nước. Nhiều gian hàng trưng bày sản phẩm đồng giá 79.000 đồng, 99.000 đồng hay 149.000 đồng, gồm áo thun, quần jeans và trang phục thường ngày, hướng đến nhóm khách trẻ có ngân sách mua sắm vừa phải.
Đang lựa chọn quần áo, chị Nguyễn Ngọc Anh (24 tuổi, ngụ phường Bến Thành, TP.HCM) cho biết tranh thủ ghé nhiều cửa hàng để tìm mua trang phục giảm giá.
Quà Tết năm nay, doanh nghiệp đặt tiêu chí thiết thực và tiết kiệm
Hàng hiệu giảm đến 80%, quần áo đồng giá từ 199k ở ngày cuối Sài Gòn Mega Sale
Đại tiệc hàng hiệu giảm đến 80% sắp đến với Vũng Tàu
"Bình thường có những mẫu áo tôi thích nhưng giá khoảng 600.000 - 700.000 đồng nên còn cân nhắc. Đợt này nhiều món giảm còn hơn 200.000 đồng, mua hai ba món cũng không quá tốn kém. Local brand Việt ngày càng có nhiều mẫu đẹp, hợp xu hướng", chị Ngọc Anh nói.
Tại The New Playground, các bảng ưu đãi 30%, 40% và 50% xuất hiện trên nhiều kệ hàng. Khách liên tục lựa chọn, thử đồ và so sánh giá, một số người tranh thủ mua nhiều sản phẩm trong đợt giảm sâu.
Anh Trần Minh Khang (27 tuổi, phường An Đông, TP.HCM) cho biết thường so sánh giá bán và chương trình ưu đãi giữa các thương hiệu Việt và quốc tế trước khi mua sắm.
"Các hãng nước ngoài có nhiều đợt giảm giá lớn, nhưng local brand Việt cũng có lợi thế về kiểu dáng, giá cả và dễ đến cửa hàng thử trực tiếp. Tôi không quá quan trọng thương hiệu trong hay ngoài nước, miễn sản phẩm đẹp, chất lượng ổn và giá hợp lý", anh Khang chia sẻ.
Cạnh tranh với nhãn ngoại không chỉ bằng giá
Nhiều khách hàng tranh thủ tìm mua quần áo giảm giá tại một cửa hàng thời trang trên đường Trần Quang Diệu - Ảnh: HÀ PHƯƠNG
Không đứng ngoài cuộc đua, các thương hiệu thời trang quốc tế như UNIQLO, H&M hay Zara cũng là những cái tên được người tiêu dùng quan tâm mỗi mùa Black Friday. Với lợi thế về độ nhận diện, hệ thống cửa hàng và nguồn lực tài chính, những nhãn hàng này có khả năng triển khai các đợt khuyến mãi trên quy mô lớn.
Để cạnh tranh, nhiều local brand Việt tập trung vào các chương trình đồng giá, ưu đãi linh hoạt và quảng bá trên mạng xã hội. Khả năng nhanh chóng cập nhật xu hướng, điều chỉnh mẫu mã theo thị hiếu người trẻ cũng giúp các thương hiệu nội địa tạo sự khác biệt, thay vì chỉ chạy đua về mức giảm giá.
Ông Lê Minh Trí, đại diện thương hiệu thời trang Việt FABRICLISM, nhìn nhận các nhãn hàng quốc tế thường có lợi thế về ngân sách và quy mô triển khai khuyến mãi. Tuy nhiên, thương hiệu nội địa có thể nhanh chóng cập nhật xu hướng, điều chỉnh chương trình phù hợp thị hiếu khách Việt.
"Chúng tôi lựa chọn tập trung vào những ưu đãi thiết thực, kết hợp với truyền thông trên mạng xã hội và hình ảnh sản phẩm thực tế để tạo sự khác biệt, thay vì chỉ thu hút khách hàng bằng những con số giảm giá", ông Trí chia sẻ.
Theo ông Trí, sức mua dịp Black Friday năm nay tăng so với ngày thường. Khách quen có xu hướng mua nhiều hơn nhờ đã trải nghiệm sản phẩm, còn người mua mới tận dụng ưu đãi để thử những mẫu mã từng quan tâm.
Ông Trí nhận định người tiêu dùng không còn dễ dàng quyết định mua hàng chỉ vì mức giảm giá hấp dẫn, mà cân nhắc nhiều hơn đến phong cách và nhu cầu sử dụng. Để giữ chân khách sau mùa khuyến mãi, FABRICLISM chú trọng phát triển các bộ sưu tập có dấu ấn riêng, đa dạng cách phối đồ.
Cuộc đua Black Friday không chỉ nằm ở mức giảm giá, mà còn là bài toán biến khách săn sale thành người mua thường xuyên. Với local brand Việt, đây cũng là cơ hội khẳng định sức cạnh tranh trước các nhãn hàng quốc tế ngay trên thị trường nội địa.
Chương trình "Vibrant HCMC - Shopping Season 2026" triển khai từ 1-11-2026 đến 5-2-2027, do UBND TP.HCM chỉ đạo. Với thông điệp "TP.HCM - Sống động từng trải nghiệm", chương trình thể hiện quyết tâm huy động các nguồn lực xã hội, kết nối các lĩnh vực thương mại, du lịch, văn hóa, thể thao, ẩm thực, giải trí, công nghệ và tài chính để thúc đẩy sức mua và tăng trưởng thương mại - dịch vụ.
Theo ban tổ chức, chỉ sau thời gian ngắn phát động, chương trình đã ghi nhận những kết quả tích cực: kết nối hơn 39 sự kiện quy mô lớn của TP và gần 300 sự kiện, hoạt động tại các phường, xã và doanh nghiệp; thu hút sự tham gia, hưởng ứng của hơn 30 tập đoàn, 66 trung tâm thương mại và trên 5.000 điểm bán lẻ; gần 100 chương trình khuyến mại lớn với tổng giá trị ưu đãi trên 250 tỉ đồng; các ngân hàng thương mại đã công bố các gói tín dụng tiêu dùng trên 10.000 tỉ đồng.
Từ nền tảng đó, TP đặt mục tiêu tổng giá trị giao dịch trên 30.000 tỉ đồng, trong đó tạo thêm từ 10.000 đến 11.000 tỉ đồng nhờ hiệu ứng kích cầu.

Black Friday deals for liquid Brazilian butt lifts criticised over safety fears | Cosmetic surgery | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Plastic surgeons say BBLs can be risky and should be performed only by trained experts.Photograph: ronstik/AlamyView image in fullscreenPlastic surgeons say BBLs can be risky and should be performed only by trained experts.Photograph: ronstik/Alamy
Black Friday deals for liquid Brazilian butt lifts criticised over safety fears
Experts say BBLs and other cosmetic procedures can be risky and seasonal offers at clinics in England could make people rush decisions
Clinics in England are promoting seasonal deals – including forBlack Friday– on liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), despite concerns about the risks of the procedure.
Thegovernment is consulting on limiting liquid BBLs, vampire facials and deep chemical peels in England to qualified healthcare professionals. The proposals follow the death of Alice Webb, a 33-year-old mother of five, after a botched liquid BBL in a Gloucester salon in 2024. Her family havecalled for laws against “cosmetic cowboys”to be introduced before more people die.
A liquid BBL involves injecting dermal filler into the buttocks. Plastic surgeons say it can carry significant risks and requires expert skill and training to perform, with large amounts of filler potentially causing serious side effects such as blood clots, fat embolisms and sepsis.
What are Brazilian butt lifts, and should they be banned?Read more
TheAdvertising Standards Authority(ASA) has already acted against time-limited promotions, concluding that Black Friday offers could rush consumers into deciding on cosmetic surgery without enough time to consider the consequences.
Between April and December 2025, the watchdog found more than 900 ads for liquid BBLs in its advert monitoring system. During that period, only 11.5% of the ads they checked stuck to the ASA’s rules.
It said some ads made claims such as “0% infection rate” or described procedures as “safe”, without properly reflecting the risks involved. Other ads played on body insecurities, promising to “boost your confidence” or “transform your body effortlessly”.
Ashton Collins, the director of Save Face, a government-approved register of accredited non-surgical treatment practitioners, said she was “outraged” by BBLs being advertised as “party-season bargains” with time-limited discounts.
“These are not routine beauty treatments; they are serious medical procedures that can lead to devastating complications,” she said.
“Marketing them this way trivialises the risks, and pressures people to make snap decisions without the time, information or proper consultation they need to make an informed choice.”
She added that Save Face had received 1,004 patient-reported complaints about non-surgical BBLs, hip-dip and breast-augmentation procedures since 2023. More than 50% of the complainants experienced sepsis, 94% required hospital treatment and 43% required surgery.
View image in fullscreenAn advert for liquid Brazilian butt lifts that was banned by the ASA in 2025 for trivialising the risks of the procedures and exploiting women’s insecurities around body image.Photograph: Advertising Standards Authority/PA
“The impact on people’s lives can be profound and lasting,” Collins said.
One London provider, Clinic Blvd, recently advertised on social media for a 48-hour deal of 800ml of filler plus 200ml free for £1,300. The post, accompanied by a picture of a woman’s bottom, stated that demand was at “an all time high” and that the deals would not be available to everyone. The clinic also listed breast filler as an option, at £799 for 400ml.
A spokesperson for Clinic Blvd said patient safety and informed consent were its top priorities. “All treatments are subject to individual consultations and clinical suitability assessments,” they said. “We take responsible advertising seriously and remain committed to maintaining appropriate professional standards.”
An Instagram post from De Vere Signature Aesthetics, also based in London, promised 100ml of free filler as a “special limited time offer” added to procedures. Their price for filler falls as the volume rises, from about £5 per ml at the bottom of the scale to about £1.50 at the top, rewarding customers for choosing larger amounts. De Vere Signature Aesthetics was approached for comment.
The Belle Clinic, also in London, advertised a deal online offering 40% off a liquid BBL in autumn to “get ready now for your Christmas party”.
A spokesperson said: “Our current promotion is an autumn and winter seasonal offer … It is not intended to create urgency or pressure anyone into making a decision about an aesthetic procedure. We take the ASA’s guidance seriously and are willing to review our promotional wording to ensure it communicates our approach responsibly.”
Nora Nugent, a consultant plastic surgeon and former president of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (BAAPS), expressed concern over time-limited discounts. “This is a sales ploy that makes people make quick decisions in case they lose out on the offer,” she said, warning that any special offers, even if not time limited, could encourage people to have treatments they might not otherwise choose.
Gerard Lambe, a consultant plastic and cosmetic surgeon and a spokesperson for BAAPS, said: “People encouraging you to have increased volumes and reduced prices, that’s the worst thing that you could ever do. [You] should never ever do that to people. It increases your risk of complications.”
However, Lambe acknowledged that some private plastic surgeons do offer deals on procedures, saying that the issue of finance is complex, and that lack of affordability could lead people to choose cheaper surgery abroad with a greater risk of complications.
The ASA said its rules made clear that adverts for liquid BBLs must be socially responsible.
“We’ve taken widespread and targeted enforcement action against advertisers breaking the rules, including by trivialising the risks of these procedures, using time-limited promotions to create a sense of urgency and exploiting women’s insecurities,” a spokesperson said.
“We support the introduction of further government measures to regulate the sector.”

Black Friday 2026: Can ChatGPT and other AI tools find you the best bargains? - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesByLiv McMahonandImran Rahman-Jones,Technology reporters
Whether it's scrolling through endless choice, spotting fake reviews, or working out if a "deal" is a deal at all, Black Friday sums up a lot of online woes.
Retailers promise bargains - but the sheer number of offers can leave us feeling no closer to finding the best deal.
It's an area where generative AI products, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, have promised to help.
But are they any good at finding Black Friday deals? We had a go ourselves a week ahead of the big day.
Figures suggest relatively few UK shoppers currently go to AI tools for help.
A recent YouGov survey of 19 countries found the UK ranked second-last in the proportion of people who said they had used AI to help them shop.
Crucially, 36% of respondents who said they would be shopping around Black Friday didn't plan to use an AI tool at all.
But the survey suggested a growing number of people were considering it - and tech firms have released features to capitalise on this.
Amazon launched Alexa for Shopping for UK users in November and OpenAI launched a Shopping Research tool on ChatGPT days before last year's Black Friday.
In the US, Google recently launched Universal Cart, with AI-powered features such as price tracking and identification of relevant promo codes.
But there has been criticism that fact-checking AI ends up taking more time, while some brands are working to try to make sure their products show up in chatbot answers.
We asked four models to find a 55-inch TV deal, using the free versions of many of the most popular tools.
While this was not a rigorous scientific test, the experience we had produced mixed results.
ChatGPT - full price and not available to buy
OpenAI's ChatGPT came up with four options.
Its top pick was a Hisense TV on Chinese retailer Joybuy's website, on sale for £499 down from £649.
The next recommendation was a 55-inch TCL-branded TV, but a sidebar showed prices for the 50-inch version, from £379 to £814.
Option three was the same Hisense TV as before, but for full price at £649 from John Lewis and Richer Sounds.
This was the "best safer purchase" according to ChatGPT, as the sites offered longer guarantee periods.
But clicking on the links did not go well. Both retailers said the TV was no longer listed online.
The fourth option was equally fruitless - another TCL TV, at full price, £150 over our budget and not available online.
At the bottom, ChatGPT served one last offer - "one OLED option to compare" - for a £1,100 LG TV thatwas marked as "Ad".
Claude - honest, but not too helpful
Claude produced the shortest answer of all the models we tested, and unlike the others, it did not give much detail on the specifications of each model.
Instead, it seemed to base its results on a small number of reviews published online.
It recommended the same two TCL TVs as ChatGPT.
But when we clicked on the links, they sent us to two dead pages on the Richer Sounds website.
Some other links led to year-old round-ups of Black Friday 2025 deals.
Claude was not very enthusiastic about its other two recommendations due to a lack of independent reviews - calling one "a decent option" but saying it "wouldn't pick" the other.
It also listed two Samsung TVs, but it told us not to buy them, with one "over budget and not clearly better than the TCLs".
We were left wondering why it even mentioned them in the first place.
Different AI model, same TV manufacturers - albeit different Hisense and TCL models to the previous chatbots' recommendations.
Gemini generated a table comparing four different models, but offered no links to the stores it named, so we searched for them ourselves.
The prices for one TCL TV were correct at £649, but it was sold out at one of the named retailers.
It said the other TCL model was available from Argos and Currys for £539 - correct for Argos, but when we checked Currys, it was £60 more expensive.
Again, it included two Samsung models to avoid due to lower screen specs.
Alexa came back with four TVs, from its own Amazon Ember at £532 to a £699 Samsung.
But its top recommendation was to go for another Samsung model at £616 (down from £749), based on its picture quality and Amazon customer rating.
Its fourth option was for a Sony TV, but it was only 50 inches, leaving us unsure why it had included it.
All the prices stated were correct, but Amazon only searches its own store. Alexa did acknowledge this, encouraging us to check its rivals for better deals, "as prices can vary" and we could get longer guarantees elsewhere.
There are methods that can boost the likelihood of getting a better response, from crafting more informative prompts to upping a chatbot's "thinking" level.
Tech journalist Alex Hughes had better luck than we did when he used ChatGPT's agentic AI mode to find a TV in last year's Black Friday sales.
Agentic AI is still in its early days, but it allows AI to act with more autonomy and carry out multi-step tasks.
The search took about 20 minutes "with very little work on my end needed,"Hughes wrote for Tom's Guide,externalin November 2025.
A year on, he told the BBC he didn't go through with buying a TV at that time.
He did later purchase one of the seven models ChatGPT had surfaced - but he had found it for a lower price in a bricks-and-mortar shop.
Will he be using AI to find Black Friday deals again this year? "Probably not," he said.
He reckoned it saved him time, but "when you're trying to deal with something like live price data... it will be inconsistent and quite often incorrect".
While we were served up the same brands again and again, in reality there are tonnes of products listed for sale around Black Friday.
Naureen Mohammed, who advises businesses on how to get their products to appear in AI results, told the BBC customers did not see the full picture when they talked to chatbots.
If businesses fail to update their prices when people start hunting for bargains, "last year's prices are served up as today's deals".
"I suspect the whole model for advertising is going to start influencing AI recommendations," she said.
Her own analysis of chatbots' Black Friday tech deals in the UK suggested the big retailers came out on top - with Amazon mentioned in half of responses, and Currys following closely behind.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future.
The 32-year-old midfielder isout of contract at the end of the season, though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028.
He was left out of the side under previous manager Michael Carrick but says he has no issues at the club and has chosen to stay at Old Trafford despite offers elsewhere in recent seasons.
He told Sky Sports:,external"The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.
"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.
"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.
"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here."
United chief executive Omar Berrada recently spoke about Fernandes' contract situation, saying: "It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private."
Fernandes has scored 75 Premier League goals since signing from Sporting in 2020 and last season set a record for the most assists in a Premier League season.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season," Fernandes said.

"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games."

The match at Anfield comes four days afterthe arrival of the Argentinian, who only oversaw his final game as United States coach on Wednesday.
The 54-year-old is tasked with ending a 13-year wait for a 21st Premier League title – only Liverpool have won the competition as many times as the Red Devils.
Unitedsacked Michael Carricklast week with the team third from bottom in the league and sufferingtheir worst league startfor 40 years.
Pochettino is the ninth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired with the club’s last league title in 2014 and he is the fourth in the last three years.
United’s recent pain is made worse by Liverpool’s revival in the last decade, with the Reds sitting fourth in the table and hoping to mount a challenge this season to move clear as the team with the most English top-flight titles.
What were the key takeaways from Pochettino’s Man United media conference?
Given the swift turnaround from his previous role to his new one, Pochettino’s unveiling as United manager was combined with the pre-game media briefing ahead of the Anfield trip.
Understandably, most of the questions centred onhow United’s form can be reversedin the short and long-term.
“It is about building our own way here,” Pochettino said when asked what he can do differently to the other managers who have taken on the role since Ferguson’s farewell. “The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday.”
“We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority.
“It is normal when you don’t win games that the confidence starts to go down,” he said. “I think the players need to feel from us that we believe and trust in them.
“With the schedule we have ahead we have to settle on our principles. The players are intelligent, they have quality. Sometimes it is unlocking some things that didn’t appear for different reasons.”
A key figure ⁠⁠⁠⁠in any rebuilding effort will be captain Bruno Fernandes, whose future has been the subject of speculation as he has ⁠⁠⁠⁠yet to agree a new deal.
Pochettino revealed he had already held extensive talks with the Portugal midfielder and indicated he remained central to his plans.
“Bruno is our captain and a very important player but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top,” he said.
“We spoke, I spent three hours chatting with all the players individually. It was ⁠⁠⁠⁠very nice contact.”
Questions about the squad’s fitness levels have swirled around Old Trafford, but Pochettino refused to criticise what he had inherited.
“It is about proposing that idea to be brave and take it to the field,” he said.
“We ⁠⁠⁠⁠cannot talk about data without context. It is easy to manipulate data but we need to ⁠⁠⁠⁠be honest, sometimes they don’t show something that you can see on the field.
“We are here not to denounce things. We are here to build something with our players.”
What have Liverpool said ahead of Manchester United’s visit?
Liverpool had lost consecutive games before their 3-1 win against bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace in their last match.
The run summed up the mixed start to life at Anfield for Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer – the former Bournemouth manager admits an epic encounter awaits.
“You don’t find bigger games than this, honestly. I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be part of these games,” Iraola said.
“We have to acknowledge the importance of the game, and also a lot of ingredients, such as their new manager.
“It is important for us in lots of different ways because we want to improve our form at home and the first chance we have to do that is on Sunday.”
Iraola also admitted he fears Pochettino, whose Premier League experience was gained at Tottenham and Chelsea, will have an advantage because he does not know the Argentinian’s preferred tactics with his new club.
“We’ve faced each other. Obviously he has a lot of Premier League games that we can look at and we can look at games in the US, but they still have this small advantage,” Iraola said.
“We don’t have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don’t actually know.
“The staff have been working with them, so they are going to arrive well prepared. We don’t have the references that we have against other teams.”
Iraola will have to adapt on the fly and the Spaniard plans to switch up his game plan if he is caught out by Pochettino’s tactics.
“Especially the beginning of the game will be important as we have to adapt to certain things and manage the situation as quick as possible,” he said.
“Every time there is a new manager you want to impress. It happens everywhere. But we have been focusing more on us, how we can improve.”

Three issues Mauricio Pochettino must address at Man United: Can the new boss get Bruno Fernandes going?
As Mauricio Pochettino gets ready to make hisManchester Uniteddebut, the rot at the legacy Premier League club is running deep.
Since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in the summer of 2013, Manchester United has been a breeding ground for toxicity, dysfunction, and a comedy of errors. They have not won a single Premier League title since then, with two second-place finishes and three third-place finishes, plus a whopping seven times finishing fifth or below.
With United now sitting 18th through the first 10 matches of the 2026/27 season, and manager Michael Carrick sacked just months after signing on as permanent boss in the summer, in comes Pochettino to save the club.
The Argentine called it his "dream job" but there's a lot of work to do. Here's the biggest areas where Pochettino can turn his focus to reverse United's fortunes in the short-term.
MORE:Why Arsenal will win the Premier League title
Three issues Mauricio Pochettino must address at Manchester United
There are a whole host of problems at Manchester United that Mauricio Pochettino has to address, some more important than others.
Here are three key areas where Pochettino can focus his attention from the beginning to help turn the Red Devils around.
MORE:Ruben Amorim gushes about USMNT star Christian Pulisic
Get Bruno Fernandes back to last season's creative form
This is the most obvious point that Mauricio Pochettino must address quickly at Manchester United.
For years, fans asked "where would Man United be without Bruno Fernandes?" Well, we're finding out this season. Now 32 years old, Fernandes has four goals so far this campaign, but three of those came way back on August 30 in a hat-trick againstIpswich Town— ironically, United's last Premier League victory.
More importantly, Fernandes' creative contributions have cratered. He has just 15 chances created, or slightly under 1.5 per 90 minutes. That is a cavernous decline from his record-setting 2025/26 season, where he assisted 136 shots, or about 3.89 per 90 minutes. That year, Fernandes equaled the Premier League record for assists with 21, but he has just two measly assists through nine appearances so far this season.
Pochettino must figure out how to get United's most dangerous attacking player back to his best in the build-up, or nothing else will matter.
Figure out how to effectively get Man United to press without falling apart
This season, Michael Carrick has been unable to figure out a way to get Manchester United players to press effectively without conceding a glutton of opposition chances on the other end.
Carrick's tactics in the 2026/27 season have been incredibly passive, a noticeable shift from his time as interim manager last season.
Last season, according toanalytics website MarkStats, Man United had the sixth-best mark (80.4%) in the Premier League for opponent buildup pass completion percentage outside of the final third, putting their opponents under pressure and making it difficult for them to build up into the attacking phase of play. It's hard to differentiate how much of that was credited to the first half when Ruben Amorim was in charge, but the number is good enough that a half-season of blatantly passive season clearly has not soiled it much.
This season, the number is 82.4%. On its own, that's not too bad, even if it drops Man United to 13th-best in the Premier League in that category, explaining how they allow opponents to come at them willingly, but it's only half the story — United don't generate turnovers either.
Man United are generating just 17.9 opposition turnovers in the attacking third per match, meaning they don't pressure their opponents in the danger zone. They also have the Premier League's second-worst opposition pass completion percentage in the fist 10 seconds after losing the ball, indicating they have an extremely poor counter-pressing ability.
Mauricio Pochettino is famous for his pressing — not necessarily an all-out, overwhelming pressing assault, but a strictly-defined pressing structure in which his players know the triggers and can execute it without sacrificing the team's defensive capabilities. It will be up to Pochettino to implement his style quickly if he is to turn this team around before things spiral further out of control.
The Argentine said coaching in international football made him a "more complete" coach, because it taught him how to implement tactics and philosophies quickly when given very little training time. That will be put to the test almost immediately.
Stem the toxic dressing room atmosphere
Off the field, Manchester United have been an absolute mess over the last few years, and it has progressed to toxic levels.
A few weeks ago, Carrick was forced to address an embarrassing situation as he was called out by Bruno Fernandes, the club captain, for his tactical approach. Regardless of who was in the right, a public spectacle of such negativity is not the atmosphere that fosters success.
United has also been subjected to numerous dressing room leaks over the years since Sir Alex Ferguson departed, as the fractured atmosphere has been a constant feature of the club.
Like he successfully did at the United States federation when he first joined, Pochettino has to build a culture of togetherness at Manchester United, from the dressing room to the staff and beyond. It will be an extremely difficult task, given the toxic relationship between the fanbase and ownership, with the squad stuck in between.

Kyle specializes in soccer tactics and betting, with a degree in data analytics. Kyle also does TV broadcasts for Wake Forest soccer and has had previous stops with NBC Soccer and IMG College. When not covering the game, he has long enjoyed loyalty to the New York Giants, Yankees, and Fulham. Kyle enjoys playing racquetball and video games when not watching or covering sports.

Closer EU ties will give UK say on Brussels decisions, says Ed Miliband | Brexit | The GuardianSkip to main contentSkip to navigation
Ed Miliband: ‘We’ve got to lay out the options.’Photograph: Nicolas Tucat/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEd Miliband: ‘We’ve got to lay out the options.’Photograph: Nicolas Tucat/AFP/Getty Images
Closer EU ties will give UK say on Brussels decisions, says Ed Miliband
Foreign secretary says there is clear case to integrate more closely but does not say if he backs talks on possibly rejoining
Closer links with the EU will mean the UK having a say on decisions made by Brussels, Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has argued as ministers faced pressure to move further afterFriday’s landmark dealwith the EU.
Any timetable for closer integration, including possible talks about the UK rejoining the EU, remains unclear after the Brussels summit, with Andy Burnham saying he would now “brainstorm” over future ties.
Emily Thornberry, the Labour MP who chairs the Commons foreign affairs committee, said Burnham should now push for membership.
“The problem with being outside the bloc is that we end up in a permanent state of negotiation, because we always have to play catchup, rather than having a seat at the table,” she wrotein an articlefor the Sunday Mirror. “That’s why I think we should simply be back in the European Union.”
Speaking to BBC One’s Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg show, Miliband refused to say whether he now supported discussions on potentially rejoining, but said the deal reached at Friday’s summit – on food and drink, emissions trading and a mutual youth mobility scheme – showed the benefits of closer links, including UK input to EU regulations that were being followed anyway.
“At the moment, what the situation is is that we are essentially rule takers,” he said. “Businesses are rule takers if they want to sell into the European market. So they have to abide by the rules of theEuropean Union, but at the same time, because we are not integrated into that market for food and agricultural products, they have to fill in a whole bunch of forms.”
He said this was “the worst of all worlds” and it meant there was a clear case to integrate more closely into EU markets.
Another reason for even closer ties, he said, was the transformed geopolitical order since 2016, including Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the US’s distancing from Europe under Donald Trump.
He said: “I was not in favour ofBrexit, as you know, but I accepted the result, and I think it was right to accept the result. [But] I think there’s a key point: the world has changed massively since 2016, and we can’t stand still.
“How can we say ‘well, this is all it is, the status quo is fine, even with the summit today. We’re not even going to look at the future of our relationship with the European Union.’ Of course, we’ve got to do that, and we’ve got to lay out the options.”
Theresa May ‘aghast’ at Andy Burnham’s talk about rejoining EURead more
Speaking for the Conservatives on the Sunday morning broadcast round, Alex Burghart, Kemi Badenoch’s deputy, said Burnham should simply be concentrating on better defence ties with Europe, arguing that the public would not want to return to the EU.
Asked if the Conservatives would undo the deal made at Friday’s summit if they won power, Burghart said they would. He said: “Yes, we would scrap it. I don’t think that there will be good outcomes from it. And I also don’t think it is a good idea for a country like Britain to hand over control of its rules to another power and have no say over how those rules are created right into the future. This is a silly idea.”
Burnham faces some nervousness in his cabinet and the parliamentaryLabourparty more widely over talk of possibly rejoining, with some MPs wary about the bitter political fight this could set off.
But Thornberry in her article praised Burnham for having “finally ended the conspiracy of silence over Brexit”, saying polls indicated that a majority of the UK public now backed rejoining.

Andy Burnham: UK to explore even closer ties with EU after agreeing deal - BBC News
Image source,EPA/ShutterstockImage caption,
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Council President Antonio Costa join hands at the end of a press conference during the EU-UK summit in Brussels
Andy Burnham said the UK will discuss possible options for even closer ties with the EU, after agreeing a deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.
The prime minister said it was a "good day" for Britain and Europe, adding the Treasury believes the deal could boost the UK economy by up to £17bn a year.
European Council President António Costa said the EU remains "open to have the closest possible relationship" with the UK.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal "isn't fair" - and Reform's Nigel Farage called it a "betrayal of the British people".
Legislation to implement the deal is expected to be introduced in the UK Parliament next week.
Burnham arrived in Brussels to finalise the latest stage of the government's post-Brexit "reset" of relations with the EU, which originally began under former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.
The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028.
The UK government believes the changes will cut costs for businesses and could bring prices down for shoppers, while critics argue the change will make the UK a "rule taker" from Brussels rather than a rule maker.
Watch: What the new UK-EU deal could mean for European relations
The new youth experience scheme will allow up to 100,000 18 to 31 year olds from the EU to travel, work and study in the UK for up to three years. The same number of young Britons will be allowed into Europe.
The two sides want to ensure that opportunities under the annual scheme will be available to young people by no later than January 2030.
A further six months is available to discuss a deal on tuition fees, which could prove to be a potential stumbling block.
There have been calls from the European side for fees to be reduced for EU students at British universities. The joint statement says any agreement would also be for UK students in the EU.
Burnham gets his first taste of EU dealmaking and seems hungry for more
What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?
Faisal Islam: This cost-cutting UK-EU deal doesn't mean lower prices will follow
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she is "confident" a solution will be found, with Burnham adding: "Me too."
On immigration, the UK and EU have committed to working closely to tackle migrant smuggling and human trafficking. They also expect their law enforcement agencies to share more data.
Burnham said "significant progress" has been made to help "disrupt the gangs who are making those dangerous crossings across the English Channel".
The UK-EU statement also said talks on linking the EU and UK emissions trading systems have concluded and they aim to apply the agreement from 2028.
Watch: Will the UK-EU summit deal boost the economy?
Burnham argued that polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".
He added: "Beyond that we do need to consider what is the right long-term relationship. Incremental steps only take us so far."
The prime minister said his government will publish a 10-year plan next month, adding it will set out its ambitions for reindustrialisation, growth in "all parts of Britain" and opportunities for young people.
Burnham said these ambitions are "connected to our long-term relationship with our nearest partner".
He said over the coming months before the next UK-EU summit both sides will "seek to conduct an informal brainstorming process" to look at what those options are.
Burnham added: "What we are announcing today is probably the limit of what we can achieve in this Parliament, given what needs to be done to implement it.
"But we want to inform the Parliament after this one, so that decisions can be taken about that long-term relationship."
Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledged there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement", and Burnham has committed to this.
The prime minister said the "British people will be the boss of what happens next", with the next election needing to be held by August 2029.
Von der Leyen, who said the summit was a "turning point" for the EU-UK relationship, said "we are open for brainstorming".
Badenoch said the deal was not fair because UK farmers would now have to follow rules made by Brussels and more young people will come to the UK to "compete with our young people who are struggling to get jobs".
Badenoch was also asked about the Treasury's analysis, which Burnham said suggested the deal "will add up to 0.5%" to UK gross domestic product and he described it as a "£17bn boost to the British economy".
She claimed Burnham has "plucked that figure out of the air" and "the only modelling I've seen that even talks about that figure says it's actually 0.0%".
Farage said Friday was a "very good day for the EU", adding: "A good day to try and humiliate the one member state that actually had the courage to say, 'We don't need to be part of you, we can govern our own country'."
In a social media post, Farage, who was a leading figure in the 2016 campaign to get Britain out of the EU, added: "Like every prime minister before him, Burnham is a total fraud. Only Reform will stop the endless betrayal of the British people."
Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said there needed to be more than "tweaks" to the UK's relationship to the EU.
"A youth mobility scheme is a big step forward, but it's nowhere near enough. We need a whole new deal that actually works for Britain, and fast."

Theresa May 'aghast' at Burnham's EU plans and says 'Brexit is done' - BBC News
Watch: Theresa May says Burnham must 'accept Brexit and move on'
Published22 November 2026, 06:01 GMT
Former Prime Minister Theresa May has warned Andy Burnham he should "move on" from Brexit, telling the BBC she is "aghast" the prime minister could be considering rejoining the EU.
At the Brussels summit this week the PM said he wanted to "brainstorm" options for the future relationship between Britain and the trading bloc.
In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Baroness May, who spent three years negotiating an EU exit deal, said: "Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."
May claimed Burnham "wants to pat people on the head" by suggesting: "Remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you. So have another go and come out with the right answer."
May, who was prime minister between 2016 and 2019 urged Burnham to "just get on with" today's challenges rather than re-opening the conversation around being in the European Union.
Before becoming PM she had campaigned to stay in the EU, but when in No 10 she presided over three years of tortuous negotiations.
The deal she concluded was rejected by MPs. She was forced to quit and was replaced by Boris Johnson in 2019.
Telling Burnham to "move on", she said: "What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours that have to be put in - it's across the whole of government.
"It's not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers' time, officials' time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations. Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you're getting out what you want.
"And that's one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU. And also we, as a country, we voted for Brexit.
"When I was prime minister I was very clear, we should deliver on that vote. So I'm afraid my message to him really is, you know, people voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."
Warning against another vote, May told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "I almost think this is what Andy Burnham is saying to the British people, sort of patting them on the head.
"He wants to pat them on their head and say, you know what, remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you? So have another go and come out with the right answer.
"Or what he thinks is the right answer. But as I say, let's just get on with making sure the UK is as strong economically, in security terms, and in terms of opportunities for people as it can be."
Speaking to the BBC back in 2023, she said the UK "would have been better off if MPs had backed her deal to leave the European Union".
Her deal had included the prospect of a vote on holding a second referendum, and a vote on a temporary customs union, as well as promises on workers' rights and environmental protection.
May claimed her plan was thwarted by "hardline" Brexit-supporting MPs and those who wanted to remain in the EU.

UK should only rejoin EU if it innovates on technology, Blair warns
On Saturday, Sir Tony Blair - another former prime minister -weighed inon the UK's future relationship with the EU.
Speaking toThe Sunday Times,external, Sir Tony has said Britain should only rejoin the EU if it reforms - and allows more innovation on technology.
Sir Tony, a prominent opponent of leaving the EU, told the paper: "I do think Brexit was a real mistake."
But he added the debate was different now than it was in 2016.
Referencing the need for technology innovation, he said Europe could and "probably are" moving in the wrong direction.
It comes after Burnham struck a deal with the EU in Brussels on Friday, covering British food exports, emissions trading anda youth experience scheme.
The prime minister also said that over the coming months before the next UK-EU summit both sides will "seek to conduct an informal brainstorming process" to look at the options for their long-term relationship.
He has previously suggested potential options for the future could include rejoining the customs union, the single market or a fresh referendum on full EU membership.
However, Burnham has ruled out major changes to the UK-EU relationship before the next general election, saying he will stick to Labour's 2024 manifesto pledge not to return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement.

While he’s voiced support for re-joining the bloc, he’s also stressed that all options are on the table and there’s a long road ahead in convincing the British public and securing the unanimous assent needed from the 27-nation bloc.
Critics have piled in this morning, warning how tricky of an endeavour this could be. Ex-PMTheresa May, whose government was brought down by Brexit in 2019, has told the BBC that the divorce “is done” and he should “move on”.
That interview’s coming up on Laura Kuenssberg’s show later this morning. Meanwhile over on Sky, BrexiteerMichael Goveis hosting Reform and Tory naysayers as well as the European relations minister. I’ll recap their comments.
European Relations Minister Hamish Falconer on Sky this morning criticised the post from earlier this week, where the US president shared a picture of him embracing Putin under the caption “My Friend”.
Falconer said Putin was a “butcher” and “not a friend of the UK”.
One area where the UK is absolutely and completely united across the whole political spectrum is standing with Ukraine against Russia’s barbaric, illegal war.
So would VladimirPutinbe my friend? No. And he’s not a friend of the UK either.”
He saidAndy Burnhamhad also made the UK’s position clear to Trump.
The Prime Minister speaks to the president regularly, and is in absolutely no way pulling his punches about the strength of feeling that the UK has as a whole about Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Tory deputy leader Burghart and Reform’s deputy Tice also condemned Trump’s post.
“I’m sad and I’m depressed because you know the world that I grew up in was one in which the United States was a defender of freedom, and I worry that we might be moving into a world where that isn’t the case.
Ticesaid Trump’s post was “wrong at every level”.
It’s a grave mistake. He is not our friend, Putin. He is, as others have said, a murderous dictator and no-one is in any doubt about that.

Critics of the youth mobility deal have mainly focused on the idea of an “influx” of European youth competing with Brits for jobs when there’s this ongoing Neets crisis.
Roughly one million 16-24 year-olds in the UK aren’t in education, employment or training (Neet).
Miliband on the BBC, points out that the UK already has such youth mobility deals with several countries, and the offer goes both ways.
There’ll be young people from Britain going to work in Europe, and study, and live, and there’ll be young people from Europe coming to our country as well.
I absolutely believe we can both address the issue of Neets, which I think Alan Milburn did excellently this week, and we can address the issue of young people having the freedom to go and work and live in Europe.
I think young people have got a really raw deal over the last decade, and it starts to put it right.
View image in fullscreenBritain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham, First Secretary of State Louise Haigh, Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs Secretary Ed Miliband, Business and Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds and Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey attend the EU-UK summit, on November 20, 2026 in Brussels, Belgium.Photograph: WPA/Getty Images
The Tories and Reform have made the argument this morning that the new food deal is “bad” for British farmers, because they will be subject to EU rules and standards.
They say more than 90% of British farmers currently don’t export to the EU- so why should Britain have to cede that control over standards?
The government’s response to this is that well, at the moment, farmers who sell into the EU already have to comply by the rules and also fill out loads of forms to prove they’re matching the standards.
“This is why it’s the worst of both worlds. We have to abide by the rules and fill in all the forms. What is the point of that?” says Ed Miliband on the BBC.
What we’re saying is that actually, yes, we should integrate into the market where for the first time, we’ll be able to shape decisions agreed to in the EU.
Reform UK’s deputy leaderRichard Ticehas also slammed the new EU agreements as “a really bad deal”.
He says “it’s not a reset, it’s a reverse” and claims that it won’t add to GDP but actually reduce GDP. The government says it could lead to a 0.5% bump.
Tice doesn’t elaborate on details here, or where that cost will come from but it appears his argument is: “The extra burdens of EU regulations that will be forced through dynamic alignment across all UK businesses is way more than that small net benefit.”
“Yes, a few exporting food businesses may benefit. But what about all the bakers in Boston and Skegness and elsewhere in the country who don’t export to the EU who will then have to suffer dynamic alignment amongst hundreds of thousands of other UK businesses that don’t export.”

Lincolnshire, United Kingdom –A decade is a short time in cheesemaking. Barrels of Tim Jones’ “Lincolnshire Poachers” cheese rest on their racks for months and years, disturbed only by Florence, the robot cheese turner.
Complexity, depth and flavour develop with patience.

The most mature cheese in Tim’s Lincolnshire dairy, in the English midlands, is five years old. By that measure, it was only a couple of cheeses ago that 52 percent of the British public voted for the country’s most tumultuous constitutional revolt in living memory.
Jones was one of them. But he is under no illusion that it went well – particularly for his exports.
“It suddenly made life much harder. We lost certain customers, and it became more expensive to get the cheese there. It definitely harmed our business,” he told Al Jazeera.
Ten years after the UK voted to leave the European Union, few are happy with what they got.
Jones, a Brexit voter, has some regrets about his decision [Al Jazeera]
Remainers are still heartbroken that a majority of the country did not look on EU membership with approval. Leavers, by and large, think many of Brexit’s promised benefits were never delivered.
“I did vote to leave,” said Jones. “But I didn’t vote to leave in the way that we did.”
Recent polling tells a consistent story: A majority of Britons now view Brexit as a mistake.
In September, 55 percent of respondents told YouGov that leaving the EU was a wrong turn for the UK. Only 21 percent think it was the right decision.
Fifty-nine percent of Britons now support rejoining the EU.
The relatively new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has noticed the shift in public mood. Less cautious than his predecessor, Keir Starmer, Burnham reignited the Brexit debate shortly after taking office in July.
He has ruled out major changes to the UK’s relationship with the EU before the next general election. But he would like to see the country back in the bloc within his lifetime, and has suggested that a future Labour manifesto could promise a new referendum.
The changing mood is only part of the logic. A government searching for growth would naturally prioritise what is still its biggest trade partner. Geopolitics matter too. The UK’s bond with the United States is less reliable than it was.
Unsurprisingly, Brexit talk has swept through media in Britain and, to a lesser extent, in Europe. Burnham insists he will not get ahead of the public on this. His immediate concern, he says, is improving the current UK-EU relationship.
On Friday, Burnham will be in Brussels for the second UK-EU Summit – a vehicle established under Starmer to deepen post-Brexit cooperation.
Among the deals being worked on are a youth mobility scheme, an emissions trading agreement, and a food and drink trade deal.
Jones, the Lincolnshire cheesemaker, is hopeful.
“If he can reduce the red tape and the cost of sending cheese to Europe – and for us that means across the world – that would be a huge positive for us,” he said – although he was less certain which way he would vote in another referendum.
“Gosh, I genuinely don’t know. I think it would depend entirely on a critical view on the arguments that were presented at the time. A much more critical view than I had the first time around.”
It is an issue familiar to anyone who has lived through the Brexit years: the terms matter.
Former premier Theresa May used the motto, “Brexit means Brexit”. But the slogan was vague. What kind of Brexit? Hard? Soft? Norway Plus? Canada Plus?
There were many potential Brexits – as there might be many possible ways to rejoin.
A new YouGov survey gave people a menu of 18 options.
In the most popular scenario, 58 percent said they would vote to rejoin if the UK stayed out of the euro, joined the border-free Schengen Zone, and kept its previous rebate from the EU budget. But if the UK lost the rebate, did not join Schengen, and adopted the euro, only 35 percent of people said they would be interested in EU membership.
Anticipating the battles ahead, two pro-Brexit campaign groups are relaunching under new names: Stay Out and Enough Official.
Burnham says he will begin talks with the EU about options for the long-term relationship after this week’s summit.
Buckle up, the Brexit wars may be starting again.

fact_units.text: Theresa May 'aghast' at Burnham's EU plans and says 'Brexit is done' - BBC News
Watch: Theresa May says Burnham must 'accept Brexit and move on'
Published22 November 2026, 06:01 GMT
Former Prime Minister Theresa May has warned Andy Burnham he should "move on" from Brexit, telling the BBC she is "aghast" the prime minister could be considering rejoining the EU.
At the Brussels summit this week the PM said he wanted to "brainstorm" options for the future relationship between Britain and the trading bloc.
In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Baroness May, who spent three years negotiating an EU exit deal, said: "Brexit is done.
May claimed Burnham "wants to pat people on the head" by suggesting: "Remember that vote?
So have another go and come out with the right answer."
May, who was prime minister between 2016 and 2019 urged Burnham to "just get on with" today's challenges rather than re-opening the conversation around being in the European Union.
Before becoming PM she had campaigned to stay in the EU, but when in No 10 she presided over three years of tortuous negotiations.
She was forced to quit and was replaced by Boris Johnson in 2019.
Telling Burnham to "move on", she said: "What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours that have to be put in - it's across the whole of government.
"It's not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers' time, officials' time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations.
Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you're getting out what you want.
"And that's one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU.
And also we, as a country, we voted for Brexit.
"When I was prime minister I was very clear, we should deliver on that vote.
So I'm afraid my message to him really is, you know, people voted for Brexit.
Warning against another vote, May told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "I almost think this is what Andy Burnham is saying to the British people, sort of patting them on the head.
"He wants to pat them on their head and say, you know what, remember that vote?
But as I say, let's just get on with making sure the UK is as strong economically, in security terms, and in terms of opportunities for people as it can be."
Speaking to the BBC back in 2023, she said the UK "would have been better off if MPs had backed her deal to leave the European Union".
Her deal had included the prospect of a vote on holding a second referendum, and a vote on a temporary customs union, as well as promises on workers' rights and environmental protection.
May claimed her plan was thwarted by "hardline" Brexit-supporting MPs and those who wanted to remain in the EU.
'Move on!' Former PMs pile in with advice for Andy Burnham, but will he listen?

UK should only rejoin EU if it innovates on technology, Blair warns
On Saturday, Sir Tony Blair - another former prime minister -weighed inon the UK's future relationship with the EU.
Speaking toThe Sunday Times,external, Sir Tony has said Britain should only rejoin the EU if it reforms - and allows more innovation on technology.
Sir Tony, a prominent opponent of leaving the EU, told the paper: "I do think Brexit was a real mistake."
But he added the debate was different now than it was in 2016.
Referencing the need for technology innovation, he said Europe could and "probably are" moving in the wrong direction.
It comes after Burnham struck a deal with the EU in Brussels on Friday, covering British food exports, emissions trading anda youth experience scheme.

The prime minister also said that over the coming months before the next UK-EU summit both sides will "seek to conduct an informal brainstorming process" to look at the options for their long-term relationship.
He has previously suggested potential options for the future could include rejoining the customs union, the single market or a fresh referendum on full EU membership.

However, Burnham has ruled out major changes to the UK-EU relationship before the next general election, saying he will stick to Labour's 2024 manifesto pledge not to return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement.

Khu lấn biển Rạch Giá (tỉnh An Giang) - Ảnh: CHÍ CÔNG
"Dự án lấn biển là sự đột phá để phát triển kinh tế của tỉnh trong thời gian tới. Lấn biển không giải phóng mặt bằng, không bồi thường hỗ trợ tái định cư và có nhiều dư địa về việc mở rộng diện tích đất sạch...", ông Mừng nêu rõ.

Qua kiểm tra, lực lượng chức năng phát hiện trên xe có 35 thùng xúc xích, mỗi thùng nặng 15kg, tổng trọng lượng 525kg.
Tài xế N.T.D. (SN 1991, trú tại xã Quảng Hà) không xuất trình được giấy tờ, hóa đơn chứng minh tính hợp pháp của số hàng hóa trên.
Tổ công tác đã lập hồ sơ, bàn giao toàn bộ số xúc xích cho Đội Quản lý thị trường số 2 tiếp nhận, xác minh và xử lý theo quy định.
Theo lực lượng CSGT, thời điểm cuối năm, hoạt động vận chuyển hàng hóa không rõ nguồn gốc có xu hướng gia tăng. Đội CSGT đường bộ số 3 sẽ tiếp tục tăng cường lực lượng, phương tiện kỹ thuật nghiệp vụ, tuần tra kiểm soát khép kín địa bàn và xử lý nghiêm các hành vi vi phạm trên tuyến giao thông đường bộ.
Phát hiện 12 thùng xúc xích không rõ nguồn gốc tại chợ Ka Long
Người phụ nữ bị phát hiện vận chuyển 12 thùng xúc xích không có hóa đơn, nhãn mác in chữ nước ngoài, tại khu vực gần chợ Ka Long, TP Móng Cái (Quảng Ninh).
Hà Nội: Triệt phá kho chứa 1,7 tấn xúc xích, lạp xưởng không rõ nguồn gốc
Gần 1,7 tấn xúc xích không rõ nguồn gốc, món ăn đường phố khoái khẩu của giới trẻ, vừa bị lực lượng chức năng phát hiện tại một kho hàng ở phường Từ Liêm (Hà Nội).
Thu giữ hơn 800kg lạp xưởng, xúc xích, thịt đông lạnh không rõ nguồn gốc
Cận Tết Trung thu, lực lượng hải quan tại các tuyến biên giới phía Bắc liên tiếp phát hiện, tạm giữ hơn 800kg lạp xưởng, xúc xích, thịt xiên đông lạnh và thực phẩm không rõ nguồn gốc.
Phát hiện 6 hộ kinh doanh buôn bán hàng giả mạo nhãn hiệu Adidas, Nike
Nhiều sản phẩm giả mạo các nhãn hiệu nổi tiếng như Adidas, Nike được bày bán công khai tại các hộ kinh doanh ở xã Lương Bằng (tỉnh Hưng Yên) vừa bị lực lượng chức năng phát hiện, xử lý.
